kuban-rada.s: The Kuban Rada was the elected assembly and regional government of the Kuban Cossacks, formed after the February Revolution of 1917. It declared the Kuban an autonomous and then an independent people's republic, allied uneasily with the White Volunteer Army against the…

kubrat.s: Kubrat was a Bulgar ruler of the Dulo clan who, in the 630s, threw off Avar or Turkic overlordship and united the Onogur, Bulgar and related tribes of the steppe north of the Black Sea into Old Great Bulgaria. Raised partly at Constantinople and baptised there, he was an ally…

kullervo-manner.s: Kullervo Manner was a Finnish Social Democrat, speaker of parliament in 1917, who chaired the Finnish People's Delegation, the Red government during the Finnish Civil War of 1918. After the Reds were defeated he fled to Soviet Russia and helped found the Communist Party of…

kurmanbek-bakiyev.s: Kurmanbek Bakiyev was President of Kyrgyzstan from 2005 to 2010. A former prime minister, he came to power after the Tulip Revolution overthrew Askar Akayev.

kuroda-nagahiro.s: Kuroda Nagahiro was daimyo of the Fukuoka domain in northern Kyushu from 1834 to 1869. Born into the Shimazu family of Satsuma and adopted by the Kuroda, he promoted Western learning, studying Dutch science and encouraging military and industrial improvements connected with…

kuroda-nagamasa.s: Kuroda Nagamasa was a Japanese daimyo and general, son of Toyotomi Hideyoshi's strategist Kuroda Kanbei. He served in Hideyoshi's invasions of Korea and fought for Tokugawa Ieyasu at Sekigahara in 1600, helping to win over wavering commanders.

kuroda-nagatomo.s: Kuroda Nagatomo was the last daimyo of the Fukuoka domain, succeeding his adoptive father Kuroda Nagahiro in 1869. In 1870 domain officials were found counterfeiting money, and in 1871 he was dismissed as domain governor shortly before the domains were abolished.

kurt-schuschnigg.s: Kurt Schuschnigg was Chancellor of the Federal State of Austria from 1934 to 1938, succeeding the murdered Engelbert Dollfuss. He continued the authoritarian corporate state and tried to keep Austria independent of Nazi Germany, conceding much in the July Agreement of 1936.

kyrylo-rozumovsky.s: Kyrylo Rozumovsky was the last Hetman of the Cossack Hetmanate in Left-bank Ukraine, from 1750 to 1764. The younger brother of Empress Elizabeth's favourite Oleksiy Rozumovsky, he also served as president of the Russian Academy of Sciences.

khandkya-ballal-shah.s: Khandkya Ballal Shah was a Gond king of Chanda in the Wainganga and Wardha valleys of central India. According to local tradition, he moved the royal capital from Ballarpur to Chanda, now Chandrapur, where a walled city was laid out under him and his successors.

kasym-khan.s: Kasym Khan was khan of the Kazakh Khanate from about 1511 to 1521, a son of the co-founder Janibek Khan. Under him the khanate reached its greatest early extent across the steppe and was said to number a million people.

kittur-chennamma.s: Kittur Chennamma was queen of Kittur, a small Lingayat state in northern Karnataka. When the East India Company refused to recognise her adopted son under the doctrine of lapse, she led an armed revolt in 1824 and her forces killed the British collector at Kittur.

kalachuri-chedi-era.s: The Kalachuri-Chedi era is a calendar era of ancient India whose first year began in 248 or 249 CE. It may have been founded by the Abhira king Ishvarasena, and it was later used in western India by the Traikutakas and the Kalachuris of Mahishmati and in central India by the…

kim-ryholt.s: Kim Ryholt is a Danish Egyptologist at the University of Copenhagen, known for his work on Egypt's Second Intermediate Period and on demotic literature. In his 1997 study of the period he proposed that a group of kings in the Turin King List formed a local Abydos Dynasty…

kharga-oasis.s: The Kharga Oasis is the southernmost of the major oases of Egypt's Western Desert, about 200 kilometres west of the Nile valley. It lay on the Darb el-Arbain caravan route to Sudan and has been settled since prehistoric times.

kath-khwarazm.s: Kath was the ancient capital of Khwarazm, on the right bank of the Amu Darya in present-day Uzbekistan. It was the seat of the Afrighid shahs until 995, when Ma'mun ibn Muhammad of Gurganj overthrew them, after which Gurganj became the capital.

koshamain.s: Koshamain was an Ainu chief who led an uprising against Japanese traders and settlers in southern Hokkaido in 1457, after a Japanese smith killed an Ainu youth in a quarrel. His forces took most of the Japanese strongholds on the Oshima Peninsula before Takeda Nobuhiro,…

kuril-islands.s: The Kuril Islands are a chain of volcanic islands stretching about 1,200 kilometres from Hokkaido to the Kamchatka Peninsula. Inhabited by Ainu, they were divided between Japan and Russia in 1855, and Japan received the whole chain in 1875.

kato-yoshiaki.s: Katō Yoshiaki was a Japanese daimyo and naval commander. One of the 'Seven Spears of Shizugatake' who served Toyotomi Hideyoshi, he commanded fleets in the invasions of Korea and built Matsuyama Castle on Shikoku.

ken-river.s: The Ken is a river of central India, a tributary of the Yamuna, flowing about 430 kilometres from the Kaimur hills in Madhya Pradesh through the Bundelkhand region into Uttar Pradesh. Its gorges pass through Panna National Park, and it is known for the rock formations and…

kyebi.s: Kyebi, also spelled Kibi, is a town in the Eastern Region of Ghana, the capital of the Akyem Abuakwa state and seat of its paramount chief, the Okyenhene. It lies in a gold-bearing area near the Atewa hills, and in the 20th century it became the centre of a major cocoa-growing…

kanara.s: Kanara, or Canara, is the coastal region of Karnataka, south-western India, between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea. Its ports, such as Mangalore, Bhatkal and Honnavar, traded pepper, rice and other goods with Arabia, the Persian Gulf and later the Portuguese.

kannada.s: Kannada is a Dravidian language spoken mainly in the Indian state of Karnataka, with more than 40 million speakers. Its earliest known inscription, at Halmidi, dates from around 450, and it developed a literature from the 9th century under the Rashtrakutas and later dynasties.

kachhwaha.s: The Kachhwaha are a Rajput clan who ruled Amber, later Jaipur, in Rajasthan from the 12th century until Indian independence. Close allies of the Mughals from the 16th century, they produced commanders such as Man Singh I, and Sawai Jai Singh II founded Jaipur in 1727.

kyogoku-clan.s: The Kyōgoku clan was a Japanese warrior family, a branch of the Sasaki of Ōmi province. In the Muromachi period they served as shugo governors of northern Ōmi, Izumo, Oki and Hida, but in the Sengoku period they lost power to their deputies, the Amago in Izumo and the Azai in…

kizilirmak.s: The Kızılırmak, the ancient Halys, is the longest river wholly within Turkey, flowing about 1,350 km in a wide arc across central Anatolia to the Black Sea near Bafra. In antiquity it marked the frontier between Lydia and Media, agreed after the battle of the eclipse in 585…

kaiming-dynasty.s: The Kaiming dynasty was the last royal house of the ancient state of Shu in the Chengdu plain, according to later Chinese traditions. Its founder Bieling was said to have come from the middle Yangtze region and to have received the throne after controlling a flood.

keta.s: Keta is a coastal town in the Volta Region of south-eastern Ghana, on the sandbar between the Atlantic and the Keta lagoon. A trading centre of the Anlo Ewe, it was the site of the Danish Fort Prinzenstein from 1784 and later a busy port under British rule.

kala-wewa.s: Kala Wewa is a large ancient reservoir in the North Central Province of Sri Lanka, built by King Dhatusena in the 5th century. Formed by a long earthen dam across the Kala Oya, it fed the Jaya Ganga canal, which carried water some 87 kilometres to the city of Anuradhapura.

krinjabo.s: Krinjabo is a town in south-eastern Côte d'Ivoire, near the Aby lagoon, and the royal seat of the Anyi kingdom of Sanwi. Founded by Anyi migrants from the east around the start of the 18th century, it became the centre of a state that signed protection treaties with France in…

karabakh-movement.s: The Karabakh movement was a mass Armenian movement from 1988 to 1991 demanding the transfer of Nagorno-Karabakh from Soviet Azerbaijan to Soviet Armenia. Huge demonstrations in Yerevan, led by the Karabakh Committee, turned it into a broader campaign for democracy and…

kota-cina.s: Kota Cina is an archaeological site near Medan on the east coast of North Sumatra, Indonesia. Between about the 12th and 14th centuries it was a busy trading settlement, where excavations have found large quantities of Chinese ceramics and coins and Buddhist and Hindu statues…

kinkaku-ji.s: Kinkaku-ji, the Temple of the Golden Pavilion, is a Zen temple in northern Kyoto, Japan. It began as the retirement villa of the shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu, who built the gold-leafed pavilion from 1397; after his death in 1408 it became a temple.

kakuyids.s: The Kakuyids were a Daylamite dynasty that ruled in western and central Iran in the 11th and 12th centuries. Its founder, Ala al-Dawla Muhammad, governed Isfahan and Hamadan from about 1008, and the philosopher Avicenna served at his court.

korce.s: Korçë is a city in south-eastern Albania, on a plateau near the borders with Greece and North Macedonia. A centre of the Albanian national awakening, it saw the opening of the first Albanian-language school in 1887.

kalka-shimla-railway.s: The Kalka–Shimla Railway is a narrow-gauge mountain railway in northern India, opened in 1903 to link Kalka on the plains with Shimla, the summer capital of British India. About 96 km long, it climbs through more than 100 tunnels and over more than 800 bridges.

kalaburagi.s: Gulbarga, officially Kalaburagi since 2014, is a city in northern Karnataka, India. Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah made it the first capital of the Bahmani Sultanate in 1347, and it remained the capital until the court moved to Bidar in the 1420s.

kaditshwene.s: Kaditshwene was the capital of the Bahurutshe, a large stone-walled Tswana town on a hill near present-day Zeerust in South Africa's North West province. When the missionary John Campbell visited it in 1820 he estimated its population at 16,000 and admired its metalworking and…

kweneng-district.s: Kweneng District is a district of south-eastern Botswana, north-west of the capital Gaborone, whose name means place of the Kwena. It covers the traditional territory of the Bakwena chiefdom and has its administrative centre at Molepolole.

kocel.s: Kocel was a Slavic prince of Lower Pannonia, the son of Pribina, who ruled from Mosapurc near Lake Balaton as a vassal of the East Frankish kings from 861 to about 876. He welcomed the Byzantine missionaries Cyril and Methodius in 867 and supported their Slavonic liturgy, and…

krsto-frankopan.s: Krsto Frankopan was a Croatian nobleman of the powerful Frankopan family and a leading commander against the Ottomans. In 1525 he relieved the besieged fortress of Jajce in Bosnia, then a key Hungarian stronghold on the frontier.

khaleda-zia.s: Khaleda Zia, the widow of President Ziaur Rahman, became leader of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party in 1984 and joined the movement that ended Hussain Muhammad Ershad's rule in 1990. She was Bangladesh's first woman prime minister, serving from 1991 to 1996 and from 2001 to…

kanye.s: Kanye is a large village in southern Botswana, the administrative centre of the Southern District and the capital of the Bangwaketse. Built on and around a defensible hill, it was re-established as the Ngwaketse capital in the 19th century under Gaseitsiwe and has remained the…

khorramshahr.s: Khorramshahr, formerly Mohammerah, is a port city in Khuzestan province, south-western Iran, at the meeting of the Karun river and the Shatt al-Arab. It was developed in the early 19th century by the Muhaysin branch of the Banu Ka'b, and under Sheikh Khaz'al it was the seat of…

kalamata.s: Kalamata is a port city in the southern Peloponnese, Greece, and the capital of Messenia. After the Fourth Crusade it became a lordship of the Villehardouin family, whose castle still overlooks the town.

kyparissia.s: Kyparissia is a town on the west coast of Messenia in the Peloponnese, Greece, on the site of an ancient town of the same name. In the Middle Ages it was called Arcadia (Arkadia) and was the seat of a Frankish barony of the Principality of Achaea, with a castle above the town.

kuomboka.s: Kuomboka ('to get out of the water') is the annual ceremony of the Lozi of western Zambia, held near the end of the rainy season when the Zambezi floods the Bulozi plain. The Litunga travels in the royal barge Nalikwanda, paddled by dozens of men to the sound of royal drums,…

kinnaur.s: Kinnaur is a mountainous district in north-eastern Himachal Pradesh, India, on the border with Tibet, crossed by the Sutlej river. Its people, the Kinnauras, combine Hindu and Buddhist traditions.

komuch.s: Komuch, the Committee of Members of the Constituent Assembly, was an anti-Bolshevik government formed in Samara in June 1918 by Socialist Revolutionary deputies of the dissolved Russian Constituent Assembly, with the help of the Czechoslovak Legion. It raised a People's Army…

kathua.s: Kathua is a town in the Indian union territory of Jammu and Kashmir, the headquarters of Kathua district, near the Ravi river and the border with Punjab. The district covers the lands of former hill states such as Basohli and Jasrota, which were absorbed by the Dogra rulers of…

kawus-son-of-kavad-i.s: Kawus was the eldest son of the Sasanian king Kavad I and ruled Tabaristan and the Caspian provinces as a sub-king in the early 6th century. When his younger brother Khosrow I was chosen to succeed their father in 531, Kawus claimed the throne and was defeated and executed.

kinshasa.s: Kinshasa is the capital and largest city of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, on the south bank of the Congo River opposite Brazzaville. It was founded in 1881 by Henry Morton Stanley as a trading post named Léopoldville after King Leopold II, and became the capital of the…

kabylia.s: Kabylia is a mountainous region of northern Algeria east of Algiers, home to the Kabyle Berbers. It is divided into Greater Kabylia around the Djurdjura range and Lesser Kabylia to the east, around Béjaïa.

kapudan-pasha.s: Kapudan Pasha was the title of the grand admiral of the Ottoman navy, from the 16th century one of the highest officials of the empire. Besides commanding the fleet, the Kapudan Pasha governed the Aegean islands and coastal districts that supported the navy, as head of the…

kashkadarya.s: The Kashkadarya is a river in southern Uzbekistan that rises in the Pamir-Alay mountains and flows west past Shahrisabz and Qarshi into the desert. Its fertile oases, ancient Sogdian lands, gave their name to the Qashqadaryo region of Uzbekistan.

khayr-al-din-al-tunisi.s: Khayr al-Din al-Tunisi was a statesman of Circassian origin who rose as a mamluk at the court of the beys of Tunis. A leading reformer, he presided over the council created by the 1861 constitution and set out his ideas in a famous treatise on government.

khayr-al-nisa-begum.s: Khayr al-Nisa Begum, known as Mahd-i Ulya, was a Safavid queen from the Mar'ashi family of Mazandaran. As wife of Shah Mohammad Khodabanda she effectively ran the government of Iran after his accession in 1578, but her attempts to curb the Qizilbash chiefs led to her murder by…

keoladeo-national-park.s: Keoladeo National Park is a wetland reserve next to Bharatpur in Rajasthan, India. Created in the 19th century as a duck-shooting preserve of the Maharajas of Bharatpur, it became a national park in 1982 and a World Heritage Site in 1985.

kitab-i-nauras.s: The Kitab-i-Nauras, 'book of the nine rasas', is a collection of songs written around 1600 by Sultan Ibrahim Adil Shah II of the Bijapur Sultanate. Composed in Dakhni and set to Indian ragas, the songs open with an invocation to the goddess Saraswati and praise Hindu deities…

kuressaare.s: Kuressaare, in German Arensburg, is the main town of the island of Saaremaa in Estonia. Its well-preserved castle was built in the 14th century by the bishops of Ösel-Wiek and became their main stronghold.

kneiphof.s: The Kneiphof was an island in the Pregel river in Königsberg, now Kaliningrad, and one of the three medieval towns that formed the city. It held Königsberg Cathedral, begun in the 14th century as the cathedral of the bishops of Samland, and the university.

kapara.s: Kapara was a king of Guzana, the Aramaean kingdom of Bit-Bahiani at Tell Halaf in north-eastern Syria, probably in the 10th or 9th century BCE. He built a palace whose entrance had colossal statues of deities standing on animals, and whose walls were lined with dozens of…

kermanshah.s: Kermanshah is a city in the Zagros mountains of western Iran and the capital of Kermanshah province. It lies on the ancient route from Mesopotamia to the Iranian plateau, later called the Great Khorasan Road.

kainai-nation.s: The Kainai, or Blood, are one of the peoples of the Blackfoot Confederacy, together with the Siksika and Piikani. Bison hunters of the northern plains, they signed Treaty 7 with Canada in 1877.

kalabsha.s: Kalabsha, ancient Talmis, was a town in Lower Nubia south of Aswan, known for its large temple of the Nubian god Mandulis built under the emperor Augustus. In late antiquity it was a centre of the Blemmyes, and the Nobadian king Silko recorded his victories over them in an…

kerch.s: Kerch is a port city at the eastern tip of Crimea on the Kerch Strait. It stands on the site of Panticapaeum, a Greek colony founded by Miletus around 600 BCE that became the capital of the Bosporan Kingdom, and it later passed to Byzantium, Genoa, the Ottomans and, in 1774,…

keren.s: Keren is a city in the highlands of western Eritrea and one of the country's largest towns. In 1941 it was the scene of the Battle of Keren, in which British and Indian forces broke through the strong Italian defences after weeks of fighting, opening the way to Asmara and…

kwaio.s: The Kwaio are a people of the mountains of central Malaita in the Solomon Islands, many of whom have kept their ancestral religion. In 1927 Kwaio warriors led by Basiana killed the district officer William Bell and his party while they collected the head tax, and a punitive…

kota-batu.s: Kota Batu is a historical site on the Brunei River near Bandar Seri Begawan, the capital of Brunei. It was the seat of the early sultans and is believed to have been the capital of the sultanate at its height in the 15th and 16th centuries.

kalmyks.s: The Kalmyks are a Mongolic people descended from Oirats, chiefly Torghuts, who migrated from Dzungaria to the lower Volga in the early 17th century and founded the Kalmyk Khanate under Russian suzerainty. In 1771 a large part of them, under Ubashi Khan, set out back to…

kayan-people-borneo.s: The Kayan are an Indigenous Dayak people of Borneo, living along the upper reaches of rivers such as the Kayan in North Kalimantan, the Mahakam in East Kalimantan and the Baram and Rajang in Sarawak. They were traditionally rice farmers living in longhouses under a hereditary…

kulmbach.s: Kulmbach is a town in Upper Franconia, northern Bavaria, Germany, overlooked by the Plassenburg fortress. It passed to the Hohenzollern burgraves of Nuremberg in 1340 and was the seat of the margraviate of Brandenburg-Kulmbach until the court moved to Bayreuth in the early…

kyabazinga.s: Kyabazinga is the title of the king of Busoga, in eastern Uganda. The office was created under British rule in 1919 to head the Busoga principalities as a single unit, its holder chosen from among the senior hereditary chiefs.

khatyn-massacre.s: The Khatyn massacre was the destruction of the village of Khatyn in Belarus by a German auxiliary police battalion and SS troops on 22 March 1943. Its 149 inhabitants, including 75 children, were burned in a barn or shot in reprisal for a partisan attack.

kurapaty.s: Kurapaty is a wooded area on the northern outskirts of Minsk, Belarus, where the Soviet NKVD shot and buried thousands of people between 1937 and 1941. Mass graves were uncovered in 1988, and the site became a symbol of Stalinist repression in Belarus.

key-marco.s: Key Marco is an archaeological site on Marco Island in south-western Florida, excavated by Frank Hamilton Cushing in 1896. Waterlogged muck preserved hundreds of wooden objects made by the Calusa or their predecessors, including painted masks, tools and the carved Key Marco…

kure-kastamonu.s: Küre is a town in Kastamonu province in northern Turkey, known since antiquity for its copper mines. In the late Middle Ages the mines were an important source of wealth for the Candarid beylik, which exported copper through the Black Sea port of Sinop.

kleinbasel.s: Kleinbasel, 'Little Basel', is the part of the city of Basel on the right, northern bank of the Rhine in Switzerland. Founded in the 13th century as a separate town at the end of the Rhine bridge, it was bought by the city of Basel from the bishop in 1392 and merged with it.

kimberley.s: Kimberley is a city in South Africa, capital of the Northern Cape province, founded after diamonds were found on the farms there in 1871. Its great open pit, the Big Hole, was dug by hand, and Cecil Rhodes built the De Beers company by buying up the claims.

kayapo.s: The Kayapó are Gê-speaking indigenous peoples of central Brazil. The Southern Kayapó of Goiás and Mato Grosso fought Portuguese miners and settlers in the 18th century and were largely destroyed, while the northern Kayapó, or Mebêngôkre, live today in Pará and Mato Grosso…

karnburg.s: Karnburg is a village on the Zollfeld plain north of Klagenfurt, in the Austrian state of Carinthia, the probable seat of the princes of Carantania and later a Carolingian palace. The Prince's Stone, on which new dukes of Carinthia were installed in a ceremony partly in…

khust.s: Khust is a town in Zakarpattia Oblast in western Ukraine, on the Tysa river below the ruins of a medieval castle. After the First Vienna Award gave Uzhhorod to Hungary in 1938, it became the capital of autonomous Carpatho-Ukraine.

karajia.s: Karajía is an archaeological site in the Amazonas region of northern Peru, known for a row of tall sarcophagi of clay, sticks and stones, called purunmachus, set on a cliff ledge. The figures, more than 2 metres high and topped by modelled faces, held burials of the Chachapoya…

kuelap.s: Kuélap is a walled settlement of the Chachapoya culture on a ridge above the Utcubamba valley in Amazonas, northern Peru, built mainly from about the 6th century CE. Its massive limestone walls, up to about 20 metres high, enclose more than 400 round stone buildings.

kanhadade-prabandha.s: The Kanhadade Prabandha is an epic poem in Old Western Rajasthani, the ancestor of Gujarati and Rajasthani, composed by the poet Padmanabha in 1455. It tells of Kanhadadeva, the Chauhan king of Jalor, and his resistance to Alauddin Khalji until the fall of Jalor in 1311,…

kanhadadeva.s: Kanhadadeva was the Chahamana (Chauhan) king of Jalor in Rajasthan at the turn of the 14th century. He resisted Alauddin Khalji of Delhi, whose armies took Siwana in 1308 and then besieged Jalor, capturing it in 1311; Kanhadadeva and his son Viramadeva were killed.

kelhana.s: Kelhana was a Chahamana king of Naddula (Nadol) in Rajasthan in the second half of the 12th century, son of Alhana. A feudatory of the Chaulukyas of Gujarat, he took part in the defence of Gujarat against Muhammad of Ghor, who was defeated at Kasahrada in 1178.

kirtipala.s: Kirtipala was a son of Alhana of Naddula who captured the hill fort of Jalor in Rajasthan from the Paramaras around 1160 and founded the Chahamana branch of Jalor, later known as the Songara Chauhans. He fought alongside the Chaulukyas of Gujarat, and the Sundha hill…

kad-koy.s: Kadıköy is a district of Istanbul on the Asian shore of the Bosporus, facing the historic peninsula. It occupies the site of ancient Chalcedon, founded by Megarian colonists in the 7th century BCE, where the Council of Chalcedon met in 451.

kirtivarman-i.s: Kirtivarman I was king of the Chalukyas of Badami from about 566 to 597, son of the founder Pulakeshin I. He defeated the Kadambas of Banavasi, the Mauryas of the Konkan and the Nalas, laying the base of Chalukya power in the Deccan.

karimnagar.s: Karimnagar is a city in northern Telangana, India, on the Manair river, a tributary of the Godavari. Its region was ruled in the 8th to 10th centuries by the Vemulavada Chalukyas, feudatories of the Rashtrakutas, and later by the Kakatiyas, the Qutb Shahis and the Nizams of…

kauthara.s: Kauthara was one of the principal regions of Champa, around modern Nha Trang in south-central Vietnam. Its chief sanctuary was the Po Nagar temple, dedicated to the goddess Yan Po Nagar, whose inscriptions go back to the 8th century.

kalinjar-fort.s: Kalinjar Fort is a hill fortress in Banda district of Uttar Pradesh, India, on the edge of the Vindhya range in Bundelkhand. One of the strongest fortresses of medieval India, it was a chief stronghold of the Chandela dynasty until Qutb al-Din Aibak took it in 1203.

kandariya-mahadeva-temple.s: The Kandariya Mahadeva Temple is the largest and most elaborate Hindu temple at Khajuraho in Madhya Pradesh, India, built around 1030 under the Chandela dynasty and dedicated to Shiva. Its soaring spire of 84 miniature towers and its hundreds of finely carved figures,…

khajuraho.s: Khajuraho is a village in Chhatarpur district of Madhya Pradesh, India, famous for a group of Hindu and Jain temples built by the Chandela dynasty between about 950 and 1050. Of some 85 temples, about 25 survive, among them the Lakshmana, Vishvanatha and Kandariya Mahadeva…

kumarapala-chaulukya-dynasty.s: Kumarapala was king of the Chaulukya dynasty of Gujarat from about 1143 to 1172, succeeding Jayasimha Siddharaja. He extended the kingdom by defeating the Chahamanas of Ajmer and the Paramaras of Malwa.

kulashekhara-alvar.s: Kulashekhara Alvar was a king of the Chera Perumals of Kerala and one of the twelve Alvars, the Tamil Vaishnava poet-saints, probably of the 9th century. His Tamil hymns, the Perumal Tirumoli, form part of the Nalayira Divya Prabandham, and the Sanskrit devotional poem…

kodungallur.s: Kodungallur is a town in Thrissur district, Kerala, near the mouth of the Periyar river on the Malabar Coast of India. Known to Europeans as Cranganore, it lies near the site of Mahodayapuram, capital of the Chera Perumals from the 9th to the 12th century, and many scholars…

kollam.s: Kollam, formerly Quilon, is a port city on the Malabar Coast of Kerala, India. It was a major centre of the medieval spice trade with Arabia and China, described by Marco Polo and Ibn Battuta, and the Malayalam calendar, the Kollam era, begins in 825 CE.

kakupakal.s: K'ak'upakal, "Fire Shield", was a lord of Chichen Itza in the second half of the 9th century and the figure most often named in the city's hieroglyphic inscriptions, which date from about 869 to 890. He appears to have shared power with relatives in a broad ruling group rather…

kailua-kona.s: Kailua-Kona is a town on the west coast of the island of Hawaiʻi, in the Kona district. It was a royal centre of Hawaiian chiefs, and Kamehameha I spent his last years there, dying at his residence of Kamakahonu in 1819.

kalaniopuu.s: Kalaniʻōpuʻu (c. 1729–1782) was ruler (aliʻi nui) of the island of Hawaiʻi from the 1750s until his death.

kealakekua-bay.s: Kealakekua Bay is a bay on the Kona coast of the island of Hawaiʻi, south of Kailua-Kona. A religious and royal centre with the temple of Hikiau, it was where James Cook anchored in January 1779 and was received with great ceremony.

kiwalao.s: Kiwalaʻō was the son and heir of Kalaniʻōpuʻu, ruler of the island of Hawaiʻi. On his father's death in 1782 he inherited the island, while his cousin Kamehameha received custody of the war god Kūkaʻilimoku.

kohala-hawaii.s: Kohala is the northernmost district of the island of Hawaiʻi, formed by the old Kohala volcano. It is the traditional birthplace of Kamehameha I and the site of Moʻokini Heiau, one of the oldest temples in Hawaii.

kona-hawaii.s: Kona is the district on the dry western, leeward side of the island of Hawaiʻi, divided into North and South Kona, with Kailua-Kona as its main town. A royal centre of the island's rulers, its slopes carried a large rain-fed field system that supported a dense population…

kaeokulani.s: Kaʻeokulani was a Hawaiian ruler of the late 18th century, a brother of Kahekili II of Maui. He became ruler of Kauaʻi through marriage to its chiefess Kamakahelei, and also held Maui for a time.

kaieiewaho-channel.s: The Kaʻieʻiewaho Channel separates the islands of Oʻahu and Kauaʻi in Hawaii and is about 115 kilometres wide, the widest channel between the main Hawaiian Islands. Its rough waters protected Kauaʻi from invasion: Kamehameha I's attempts to cross with large fleets in 1796 and…

kauai.s: Kauaʻi is the oldest and northernmost of the main Hawaiian Islands, separated from Oʻahu by the wide Kaʻieʻiewaho Channel. Its mountainous centre, Mount Waiʻaleʻale, is one of the wettest places on earth, and Waimea Canyon cuts deeply into its western side.

kekaulike.s: Kekaulike was ruler (aliʻi nui) of Maui in the early 18th century, who died around 1736. He strengthened royal power, built temples and invaded the island of Hawaiʻi, raiding the Kona coast, but was driven back.

kihapiilani.s: Kihapiʻilani was ruler of Maui in the 16th century, a son of Piʻilani. With the help of ʻUmi-a-Līloa of the island of Hawaiʻi he overthrew his elder brother Lono-a-Piʻilani and took power.

kahahana.s: Kahahana was ruler (aliʻi nui) of Oʻahu from 1773, chosen by the island's chiefs. Raised at the court of Maui under Kahekili II, he later quarrelled with him over land and had the influential priest Kaʻōpulupulu killed.

kakuhihewa.s: Kākuhihewa was ruler (aliʻi nui) of Oʻahu in the 16th century, remembered in Hawaiian tradition as a wise ruler whose reign was a time of peace and prosperity. Born at the sacred birthing site of Kūkaniloko, he is said to have held court at Kailua on the windward coast, and…

kalanikupule.s: Kalanikūpule was the last independent ruler of Oʻahu, a son of Kahekili II of Maui. On his father's death in 1794 he defeated and killed his uncle Kaʻeokulani with the help of the British trader William Brown, then tried to seize Brown's ships, killing him.

kukaniloko.s: Kūkaniloko is a sacred site near Wahiawā in central Oʻahu, Hawaii, where chiefly women came to give birth so that their children would be of the highest rank. About 180 basalt stones mark the site, some carved with petroglyphs.

katur-dynasty.s: The Katur dynasty ruled the princely state of Chitral, in the high valleys of north-western Pakistan, from the later 16th century until 1969. Its rulers took the title Mehtar, and its most powerful ruler, Aman ul-Mulk (died 1892), united upper and lower Chitral.

khowar-language.s: Khowar, also called Chitrali, is an Indo-Aryan language of the Dardic group spoken by several hundred thousand people in Chitral in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan, and in parts of Gilgit-Baltistan. It was the main language of the people and court of the princely state of Chitral…

kunar-river.s: The Kunar River rises near the Broghil Pass in the Hindu Kush and flows south-west through Chitral in north-western Pakistan, where it is known as the Chitral or Mastuj river, into eastern Afghanistan. There it passes through Kunar province and joins the Kabul River near…

kastamonu.s: Kastamonu is a city in northern Turkey, capital of Kastamonu Province, in the hills south of the Black Sea coast. Held by the Byzantines under the Komnenoi, it fell to Turkish rulers in the 12th and 13th centuries and became the seat of the Chobanids and, from 1309, of the…

kido-takayoshi.s: Kido Takayoshi (1833–1877), also known as Katsura Kogorō, was a samurai of the Chōshū domain and one of the three great leaders of the Meiji Restoration. He negotiated the Satchō Alliance with Satsuma in 1866 and helped draft the Charter Oath of 1868.

kumemura.s: Kumemura was a community of Chinese immigrants at Kume, near the port of Naha on Okinawa, founded in the late 14th century by settlers from Fujian. Its families, remembered as the "thirty-six families from Min", provided the Ryukyu Kingdom with interpreters, navigators,…

karnataka.s: Karnataka is a state of south-western India, with its capital at Bengaluru and a mainly Kannada-speaking population. It was the heartland of dynasties including the Kadambas, Western Gangas, Chalukyas, Rashtrakutas, Hoysalas and the Vijayanagara Empire, and later of the…

kingston-jamaica.s: Kingston is the capital and largest city of Jamaica, on a deep natural harbour on the south-east coast. It was founded in 1692 for survivors of the earthquake that destroyed nearby Port Royal and grew into the island's chief port and commercial centre.

kingston-ontario.s: Kingston is a city in Ontario, Canada, at the eastern end of Lake Ontario where it flows into the St. Lawrence River.

kibushi.s: Kibushi is the Malagasy language spoken in Mayotte, closely related to the Sakalava dialect of north-western Madagascar. It was brought by Malagasy settlers who came to the island over several centuries.

kalinago.s: The Kalinago, also known as the Island Caribs, are an Indigenous people of the Lesser Antilles, who lived on islands such as Dominica, Saint Vincent, Guadeloupe and Martinique when Europeans arrived. They were skilled seafarers who fought fiercely against Spanish, French and…

kingstown.s: Kingstown is the capital and chief port of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, on the south-west coast of Saint Vincent. It developed as the seat of British colonial government after Britain gained the island in 1763, and its botanic garden, founded in 1765, is one of the oldest…

kulin.s: The Kulin are an alliance of five Aboriginal nations of central Victoria, Australia, including the Wurundjeri and Boonwurrung, whose lands cover the Port Phillip region. They share related languages and kinship ties.

king-george-sound.s: King George Sound is a large natural harbour on the south coast of Western Australia, on which the town of Albany stands. George Vancouver named it in 1791, and in 1826 Britain set up a military garrison there to forestall French claims, the first European settlement in…

kalgoorlie.s: Kalgoorlie is a city in the Goldfields of Western Australia, founded after Paddy Hannan found gold there in June 1893. The Golden Mile, one of the richest gold-bearing areas in the world, made it the centre of the region, and a pipeline from near Perth, opened in 1903,…

kansas.s: Kansas is a state of the central United States, lying on the Great Plains between Missouri and Colorado. Its grasslands were hunting grounds of the Kansa, Osage, Pawnee, Comanche and others.

kotsoteka.s: The Kotsoteka, or Buffalo Eaters, were one of the main divisions of the Comanche. They ranged over the central southern Plains, along the Canadian River in present-day Oklahoma and Texas, and like the other bands had their own chiefs and acted independently in war and trade.

kwahadi.s: The Kwahadi, or Antelope Eaters, were a division of the Comanche who lived on the Llano Estacado of the Texas Panhandle. Among the last Plains peoples to resist the United States, they fought in the Red River War of 1874–1875 under leaders including Quanah Parker.

kalinago-territory.s: The Kalinago Territory is a district on the east coast of Dominica set aside in 1903 for the island's indigenous Kalinago, or Island Caribs, and known until 2015 as the Carib Territory. Home to around 3,000 people, it is governed by an elected chief and council and holds land…

keshab-chandra-sen.s: Keshab Chandra Sen was a Bengali religious and social reformer who led the Brahmo Samaj, campaigning against caste, child marriage and for women's education and widow remarriage. He founded the Brahmo Samaj of India in 1866.

kyiv-mohyla-academy.s: The Kyiv-Mohyla Academy was a school of higher learning in Kyiv, formed in 1632 when Metropolitan Petro Mohyla merged the Kyiv Brotherhood school with his monastery school. Teaching in Latin and Church Slavonic on the model of Jesuit colleges, it became the leading centre of…

kortrijk.s: Kortrijk, in French Courtrai, is a city on the Lys (Leie) river in West Flanders, Belgium. A Roman settlement and a medieval centre of the flax and linen trade, it is known for the Battle of the Golden Spurs, fought outside its walls in 1302, when Flemish militias defeated…

kehl.s: Kehl is a town in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, on the east bank of the Rhine opposite Strasbourg, to which it is linked by bridges and a tram line. For centuries it guarded the Rhine crossing and was fortified and fought over in the wars between France and the Empire.

kocher.s: The Kocher is a river in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, about 170 km long and a right tributary of the Neckar. It rises near Aalen on the Swabian Jura and flows past Schwäbisch Hall, whose salt springs lie on its banks, through the Hohenlohe region to join the Neckar at Bad…

klodzko.s: Kłodzko, in German Glatz, is a town in Lower Silesia, south-western Poland, on the Nysa Kłodzka at the centre of a basin enclosed by the Sudetes. For centuries it belonged to the Bohemian crown, guarding the road from Silesia into Bohemia, until Prussia annexed it in 1742.

kudowa-zdroj.s: Kudowa-Zdrój is a spa town in Lower Silesia, south-western Poland, at the foot of the Table Mountains near the Czech border. Its mineral springs were known by the late 16th century, and as Bad Kudowa it became a popular health resort of the County of Glatz under Prussian rule.

kleve.s: Kleve, known in English as Cleves, is a town in the Lower Rhine region of North Rhine-Westphalia, near the Dutch border. Its Schwanenburg castle was the seat of the counts and, from 1417, dukes of Cleves, whose house also came to hold Mark, Ravenstein and Nevers.

konrad-of-marburg.s: Konrad of Marburg was a German priest and the first papal inquisitor in Germany. As confessor to Elizabeth of Hungary he imposed a harsh regime on her, and from 1231 he led a violent campaign against supposed heretics in the Rhineland and Hesse.

krak-des-chevaliers.s: Krak des Chevaliers is a Crusader castle in western Syria, on a hill commanding the Homs Gap between the coast and the interior. The Count of Tripoli granted it to the Knights Hospitaller in 1142, and they rebuilt it into one of the most formidable fortresses of the Middle Ages.

kefalonia.s: Kefalonia (Cephalonia) is the largest of the Ionian Islands, off the west coast of Greece. Byzantine until 1185, it was then ruled by Norman and Italian counts palatine, briefly by the Ottomans, and by Venice from 1500 to 1797.

knoydart.s: Knoydart is a remote, mountainous peninsula on the west coast of the Scottish Highlands, between Loch Nevis and Loch Hourn. It has no road link to the rest of the road network, and its small community at Inverie is reached by boat or on foot.

kota-kinabalu.s: Kota Kinabalu is the capital of the Malaysian state of Sabah, on the north-west coast of Borneo. Founded by the British North Borneo Company in 1899 as Jesselton, it became the capital of the Crown Colony of North Borneo after the Second World War and was renamed in 1968 after…

kalka.s: Kalka is a town in the Panchkula district of Haryana, India, at the foot of the Shivalik Hills. It is the starting point of the narrow-gauge Kalka–Shimla Railway, opened in 1903, and of the road to Shimla, the summer capital of British India, which made it the gateway to the…

konchak.s: Konchak was a khan of the Cumans (Polovtsians) in the late 12th century and a grandson of Sharukan. In 1185 he defeated and captured Prince Igor Sviatoslavich of Novgorod-Seversky, the campaign told in the Tale of Igor's Campaign, and his daughter later married Igor's son.

koten.s: Köten (Kotyan) was a Cuman khan of the early 13th century. Allied with his son-in-law Mstislav of Galich, he fought the Mongols at the Kalka in 1223, and around 1239 he led tens of thousands of Cumans into Hungary, where King Béla IV received them.

khengarji-i.s: Khengarji I was the Jadeja ruler who united Cutch in the mid-16th century and is regarded as the founder of the Cutch State. Raised at the court of the sultans of Gujarat, he overcame rival Jadeja kinsmen with their support, took the title Rao and made Bhuj his capital.

kapidag-peninsula.s: The Kapıdağ Peninsula, ancient Arctonnesus ('bear island'), is a mountainous peninsula on the southern shore of the Sea of Marmara in Balıkesir Province, Turkey. Once an island, it is joined to the mainland by a low isthmus, on which the Milesian colony of Cyzicus was built,…

khurshid-of-tabaristan.s: Khurshid was the last Dabuyid ispahbad of Tabaristan, ruling from about 740. After the Abbasid revolution he paid tribute to the new caliphate, but he rebelled in the late 750s, and in 759–760 Abbasid armies overran Tabaristan.

king-gasil.s: Gasil was a king of Gaya in southern Korea in the 6th century, usually linked with Daegaya. According to the Samguk sagi he had the gayageum, a twelve-string zither, made and commissioned the musician Ureuk to compose twelve pieces for it.

kolkata.s: Kolkata (Calcutta) is the capital of the Indian state of West Bengal, on the Hooghly River. It grew from villages where the English East India Company set up a trading settlement in 1690, was the capital of British India until 1911 and was the centre of the Bengal Renaissance.

kayseri.s: Kayseri is a city in central Anatolia, Turkey, at the foot of the extinct volcano Erciyes. As Caesarea Mazaca it was the capital of the kingdom of Cappadocia and the see of Basil the Great.

kosovo.s: Kosovo is a landlocked region in the central Balkans, with its capital at Pristina and a large Albanian majority. It was a heartland of medieval Serbia and the scene of the Battle of Kosovo in 1389, then part of the Ottoman Empire until the Balkan Wars of 1912–1913.

knockfarrel.s: Knockfarrel is an Iron Age hillfort on a ridge near Strathpeffer in Easter Ross, in the Scottish Highlands. It is one of the best-known vitrified forts in Scotland: its timber-laced stone ramparts were burnt so intensely that the stones melted and fused together.

kirrha.s: Kirrha was an ancient town on the Gulf of Corinth below Delphi, serving as the port for pilgrims to the oracle. Accused of mistreating and taxing visitors, it was destroyed by the Amphictyony in the First Sacred War in the early 6th century BCE, and its plain was dedicated to…

khalq.s: Khalq ('the masses') was the more radical of the two factions of the People's Democratic Party of Afghanistan, formed when the party split in 1967. Led by Nur Muhammad Taraki and Hafizullah Amin, it drew support from Pashtun teachers and army officers and dominated the…

kings-law.s: The King's Law (Kongeloven, or Lex Regia) was the fundamental law of absolute monarchy in Denmark-Norway, signed by King Frederick III in 1665 and published in 1709. It declared the king above all human laws and set out the succession, making it the only written constitution…

kaliakra.s: Kaliakra is a long, narrow headland on the Black Sea coast of north-eastern Bulgaria, near Kavarna, with cliffs up to 70 metres high. Fortified since antiquity, it was the capital of the 14th-century Dobrujan principality under Dobrotitsa.

kokna-people.s: The Kokna are an Adivasi people of the forested hills on the borders of Gujarat and Maharashtra in western India, especially in the Dangs, Valsad, Navsari and Nashik districts. They speak Kokni, a language related to Marathi and Konkani, and live mainly by farming.

kunming.s: Kunming is the capital of Yunnan province in south-western China, on the northern shore of Lake Dian. The lands around the lake were the heartland of the ancient Dian kingdom, and the city grew as a regional centre under the Nanzhao and Dali kingdoms and later Chinese dynasties.

karachi.s: Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan and the capital of Sindh province, on the Arabian Sea coast near the Indus delta. A small trading town in the 18th century, it grew under British rule from 1843 into a major port.

kawiil-chan-kinich.s: K'awiil Chan K'inich was the fourth ruler of the Classic Maya kingdom of Dos Pilas in Guatemala, reigning from 741. He continued his predecessors' wars across the Petexbatún region and is recorded on monuments at Dos Pilas and Aguateca.

korosten.s: Korosten is a town in Zhytomyr oblast, northern Ukraine, identified with Iskorosten, the chief town of the East Slavic Drevlians. According to the Primary Chronicle, Princess Olga burned it in 946 in revenge for the killing of her husband Igor, using birds that carried burning…

kuver.s: Kuver was a Bulgar leader of the late 7th century who rebelled against the Avar Khaganate. According to the Miracles of Saint Demetrius, he led a mixed population of Bulgars and descendants of Roman captives from Pannonia south to the Keramisian plain, near Thessalonica, in…

konstanz.s: Konstanz, in English Constance, is a city in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, on Lake Constance where the Rhine leaves the lake, on the border with Switzerland. A late Roman fort, it became a bishopric around 600, heading the largest diocese of the German lands, and later a free…

khevsurs.s: The Khevsurs are a Georgian highland people of Khevsureti, on the northern and southern slopes of the Greater Caucasus near the border with Chechnya. Living in fortified villages such as Shatili and keeping distinctive customs, dress and folk religion into the 20th century,…

kozle.s: Koźle is a historic town on the Oder in Upper Silesia, Poland, now part of the city of Kędzierzyn-Koźle. In the Middle Ages it was the seat of a small Silesian Piast duchy, and under Prussian rule it became a fortress, besieged by Napoleon's allies in 1807.

klagenfurt.s: Klagenfurt is the capital of Carinthia in southern Austria, at the eastern end of the Wörthersee. Founded in the 12th century under the Sponheim dukes, it was given by Emperor Maximilian I to the Carinthian estates in 1518 after a fire, and they rebuilt and fortified it as…

kalkar.s: Kalkar is a town on the lower Rhine in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany, founded by the counts of Cleves in 1230. It prospered from the cloth trade in the late Middle Ages, when its church of St Nicolai was furnished with carved altarpieces by a renowned school of local…

klis-fortress.s: Klis Fortress stands on a pass above Split in Croatia, guarding the route from the Dalmatian coast to the interior. It was a seat of the early medieval Croatian dukes and kings, and in the 16th century the Uskoks defended it against the Ottomans until it fell in 1537.

kovin.s: Kovin is a town in the Banat region of Serbia, on the Danube east of Belgrade. Known in Hungarian as Keve, it was a medieval fortress and the seat of Keve county in the Kingdom of Hungary, guarding a Danube crossing towards the Balkans.

konrad-i-of-glogow.s: Konrad I of Głogów was a Silesian Piast duke, a son of Henry II the Pious, who was killed by the Mongols at Legnica in 1241. First intended for the church, he received Głogów in a division of the family lands around 1251 and founded a separate duchy there.

konrad-i-of-olesnica.s: Konrad I of Oleśnica was a Silesian Piast duke, a son of Henry III of Głogów. In the division of his father's lands he received Oleśnica, east of Wrocław, and founded the Duchy of Oleśnica, which he ruled until 1366.

kalisz.s: Kalisz is a city in Greater Poland on the Prosna river, often regarded as the oldest town in Poland and identified with the Calisia mentioned by Ptolemy. In the Middle Ages it was the seat of a Piast duchy, and there in 1264 Duke Bolesław the Pious issued the Statute of Kalisz…

krzeszow-abbey.s: Krzeszów Abbey is a former Cistercian abbey in Lower Silesia, Poland, near the Czech border. Founded in 1242 for Benedictines and refounded for Cistercians by Duke Bolko I the Strict in 1292, it became the burial place of the Piast dukes of Świdnica and Jawor.

krnov.s: Krnov is a town in the Moravian-Silesian Region of the Czech Republic, on the Opava river near the Polish border, known in German as Jägerndorf. From the late 14th century it was the seat of the Duchy of Krnov, held in turn by Přemyslid, Hohenzollern and Liechtenstein dukes.

kruszwica.s: Kruszwica is a small town in Kuyavia, central Poland, on the northern shore of Lake Gopło. It was an important stronghold of the early Piast state, and in the 12th century it was the seat of a bishopric that later moved to Włocławek.

kuyavia.s: Kuyavia is a historical region of central Poland, lying west of the Vistula around Inowrocław, Kruszwica, Brześć Kujawski and Włocławek. Fertile and rich in salt, it was a core land of the early Piast state and from the 13th century was divided into small duchies under…

kvarner-gulf.s: The Kvarner Gulf is a bay of the northern Adriatic Sea in Croatia, between the Istrian peninsula and the mainland coast, with the port of Rijeka at its head. Its islands include Krk, Cres, Lošinj and Rab.

kamianets-podilskyi.s: Kamianets-Podilskyi is a city in western Ukraine, in the historical region of Podolia, built on a rocky island in a loop of the Smotrych river. Its castle, strengthened by the Koriatovich princes in the 14th century and later by the Polish crown, made it the chief stronghold…

karijotas.s: Karijotas (d. c. 1365), known in Slavic sources as Koriat, was a son of Grand Duke Gediminas of Lithuania and ruler of Navahrudak and Vawkavysk.

konstantin-stanislavski.s: Konstantin Stanislavski was a Russian actor and director who co-founded the Moscow Art Theatre with Vladimir Nemirovich-Danchenko in 1898. His productions of Chekhov's plays made the theatre famous.

kapyl.s: Kapyl (Kopyl) is a small town in the Minsk Region of Belarus, south of Minsk and north-west of Slutsk. In 1395 Grand Duke Vytautas granted Slutsk and Kapyl to Volodymyr Olgerdovich, and it remained part of the Olelkovich duchy of Slutsk and later the Radziwiłł estates.

kirchheim-unter-teck.s: Kirchheim unter Teck is a town in the Esslingen district of Baden-Württemberg, Germany, at the foot of the Swabian Jura below the castle of Teck. It was the main town of the small territory of the dukes of Teck until they sold it to the counts of Württemberg in the 1380s.

kreva.s: Kreva is a village in the Grodno Region of north-western Belarus, known for the ruins of its fourteenth-century castle, one of the oldest stone castles of the Grand Duchy of Lithuania. Grand Duke Kęstutis died there in captivity in 1382, held by his nephew Jogaila.

king-kao-of-zhou.s: King Kao of Zhou was king of the Eastern Zhou dynasty from 440 to 426 BCE, when the royal house had little power over the warring states. On his accession he enfeoffed his younger brother Jie, Duke Huan, at Henan near Luoyang, creating the Duchy of Western Zhou.

krakow.s: Kraków is a city on the Vistula in southern Poland and the country's historic capital. Seat of a bishopric from 1000, it became the coronation and royal city, with the Wawel castle and cathedral, and in 1364 Casimir III founded its university.

kimmeridge.s: Kimmeridge is a coastal village in Dorset, England, which gives its name to the Kimmeridge Clay of the Jurassic period. The local oil shale was worked from the Iron Age into the Roman period, when it was turned on lathes into bracelets and carved into furniture.

kasimbazar.s: Kasimbazar is a town near Murshidabad in West Bengal, India, which in the 17th and 18th centuries was one of the main silk markets of Bengal. The English, Dutch and French East India companies all kept factories there to buy raw silk and cloth.

kahal-zur-israel-synagogue.s: The Kahal Zur Israel Synagogue in Recife, Brazil, founded around 1636 under Dutch rule, was the first synagogue in the Americas. Its congregation was formed by Sephardic Jews, many of Portuguese origin, who came from Amsterdam.

khu-bua.s: Khu Bua is an archaeological site in Ratchaburi province in western Thailand, the remains of a moated town of the Dvaravati culture, flourishing from about the 7th to the 11th century. Excavations have uncovered brick stupas and temple bases decorated with stucco and…

kirkwall.s: Kirkwall is the main town of Orkney, on the island of Mainland in northern Scotland. It grew around St Magnus Cathedral, begun in 1137, and became the seat of the earls and bishops of Orkney, whose palaces stand beside the cathedral.

karur.s: Karur is a city on the Amaravati River, near the Kaveri, in Tamil Nadu, India. Most historians identify it with Vanchi or Karuvur, the inland capital of the early Chera kings in the Sangam age, and finds there include Roman coins and early Tamil inscriptions.

kerala.s: Kerala is a state on the Malabar Coast of south-western India, where Malayalam is spoken. It was formed in 1956 from Travancore-Cochin and the Malabar district of Madras, and its capital is Thiruvananthapuram.

kongu-nadu.s: Kongu Nadu is the historical region of western Tamil Nadu in India, around the modern cities of Coimbatore, Erode, Salem and Karur. A fertile upland crossed by trade routes between the east and west coasts, it was fought over by the Cheras, Pandyas, Cholas, Hoysalas and later…

kallanai-dam.s: The Kallanai, or Grand Anicut, is an ancient dam across the Kaveri River near Thanjavur in Tamil Nadu, India. Tamil tradition credits its construction to the Chola king Karikala in the early centuries CE, making it one of the oldest water-diversion works still in use.

karikala-chola.s: Karikala Chola was the most celebrated of the early Chola kings of the Sangam age in southern India, usually placed in the early centuries CE. Sangam poems such as the Pattinappalai praise his victory at Venni over the Chera and Pandya kings and his patronage of the port of…

khasekhemwy.s: Khasekhemwy was the last king of the Second Dynasty of Egypt, around 2690 BCE. He reunited the country after a period of division, and his name placed both Horus and Seth above it, signalling reconciliation.

kadungon.s: Kadungon was a Pandya king of southern India in the late 6th century who, according to the Velvikudi copper plates, ended the rule of the Kalabhras and restored Pandya power at Madurai. He is regarded as the founder of the First Pandyan Empire, which, with the Pallavas to the…

korkai.s: Korkai was an ancient port of the Pandya kingdom near the mouth of the Tamraparani River in modern Thoothukudi district of Tamil Nadu, India. It was the centre of the pearl fisheries of the Gulf of Mannar and traded with the Roman world, and Greek writers knew it as Kolkhoi.

kikuyu-people.s: The Kikuyu are a Bantu-speaking people of central Kenya, living around Mount Kenya, and the largest ethnic group in the country. Under British rule they lost much land to European settlers in the highlands, and Kikuyu associations led early African political protest.

kulottunga-i.s: Kulottunga I was emperor of the Chola Empire from 1070 to 1122. Born Rajendra, son of the Eastern Chalukya king Rajaraja Narendra and a Chola princess, he united the Vengi kingdom with the Chola realm on taking the Chola throne.

konark-sun-temple.s: The Konark Sun Temple is a 13th-century Hindu temple to the sun god Surya at Konark on the coast of Odisha, India, built around 1250 by the Eastern Ganga king Narasimhadeva I. It is designed as a giant stone chariot with twenty-four carved wheels drawn by seven horses.

king-kuai-of-yan.s: King Kuai of Yan was ruler of the State of Yan in north-eastern China during the Warring States period. Persuaded to imitate the legendary sage-kings, he abdicated in favour of his minister Zizhi in about 316 BCE.

kuchlug.s: Kuchlug was a prince of the Naiman, a Turkic-Mongol people of western Mongolia, who fled west after Genghis Khan's victories. Received by the ruler of the Qara Khitai, he married his daughter and seized the throne in 1211.

kutadgu-bilig.s: The Kutadgu Bilig ('Wisdom of Royal Glory') is a long didactic poem in Karakhanid Turkic written by Yusuf Balasaguni and presented to the khan at Kashgar around 1069. Framed as dialogues between a king, his vizier and a sage, it is a mirror for princes on justice, statecraft…

kang-tai.s: Kang Tai was an envoy of Eastern Wu who, with Zhu Ying, was sent by the court of Sun Quan to Funan in mainland South-East Asia in the mid-3rd century. His account of the journey, known through quotations in later works, is one of the earliest descriptions of Funan, recording…

kura-god.s: Kura was the chief god of the city of Ebla in northern Syria in the 3rd millennium BCE. Known mainly from the Ebla archive, he appears as the protector of the king and the royal family, receiving offerings in the palace and in his own temple, and his consort was the goddess…

kura-river.s: The Kura is the main river of the South Caucasus, about 1,360 kilometres long. Rising in north-eastern Turkey, it flows through Georgia, where it is called the Mtkvari and passes Tbilisi, and across Azerbaijan to the Caspian Sea, joining the Aras shortly before the coast.

khirbat-en-nahas.s: Khirbat en-Nahas, 'ruins of copper', is a large Iron Age copper-smelting site in the Faynan district of southern Jordan. Excavations led by Thomas Levy and Mohammad Najjar from 2002 dated much of its activity to the 10th and 9th centuries BCE, earlier than once believed, and…

koblenz.s: Koblenz is a city in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, at the confluence of the Rhine and the Moselle, a point marked by the Deutsches Eck monument. Founded as the Roman fort of Confluentes, it became a residence of the archbishop-electors of Trier, and in 1791–1792 it sheltered…

kalfun.s: Kalfun was the leader of the Arab and Berber soldiers, probably from North Africa, who seized the southern Italian port of Bari around 847. Some of them had served as mercenaries for the rival Lombard princes of Benevento and Salerno.

kalbid-dynasty.s: The Kalbid dynasty were Arab emirs who ruled Sicily from Palermo between 948 and 1053, first as governors for the Fatimid caliphs and later largely independently. Founded by Hasan al-Kalbi, they completed the conquest of the island and presided over a period of prosperity,…

kyk-over-al.s: Kyk-over-al is a small island in the Essequibo River in Guyana, near its confluence with the Mazaruni and Cuyuni rivers. Dutch traders from Zeeland built a fort there in the early 17th century, and it served as the seat of the colony of Essequibo until the administration moved…

klooga-concentration-camp.s: Klooga concentration camp was a Nazi labour camp in north-western Estonia, a subcamp of Vaivara, which operated from 1943 to 1944. It held mainly Jewish prisoners deported from the ghettos of Vilnius and elsewhere.

kannur.s: Kannur, formerly Cannanore, is a city on the Malabar coast of northern Kerala, India. A port of the spice trade, it was linked with the Kolathiri rulers and was the seat of the Arakkal family, the only Muslim royal house of Kerala.

kariba-dam.s: The Kariba Dam is a concrete arch dam on the Zambezi river between Zambia and Zimbabwe, built from 1955 to 1959 by the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland to supply hydroelectric power to the Copperbelt and Southern Rhodesia. Its reservoir, Lake Kariba, is among the largest…

khyan.s: Khyan was a Hyksos king of the Fifteenth Dynasty of Egypt who ruled from Avaris in the 17th century BCE. He is one of the best-attested Hyksos rulers, and objects bearing his name have been found far beyond Egypt, including an alabaster lid at Knossos on Crete and a granite…

krum.s: Krum was khan of the First Bulgarian Empire from about 803 to 814. He destroyed the remnants of the Avar Khaganate in the north-west and fought the Byzantine Empire, taking Serdica in 809.

karl-fellner.s: Karl Fellner was a Frankfurt lawyer and politician who was senior mayor of the Free City of Frankfurt when Prussian troops occupied it in July 1866. Faced with a huge Prussian war levy and threats against the city, he took his own life on 24 July 1866.

kinderzeche.s: The Kinderzeche is an annual historical festival in Dinkelsbühl, Bavaria, held each July. It recalls the legend that in 1632, during the Thirty Years' War, the town's children persuaded a Swedish colonel to spare the town.

kinzig-rhine.s: The Kinzig is a river of the Black Forest in Baden-Württemberg, flowing west through Wolfach, Haslach, Gengenbach and Offenburg to join the Rhine at Kehl. Its valley has long been one of the main routes across the Black Forest.

kinzig-main.s: The Kinzig is a river in Hesse that flows south-west between the Vogelsberg and the Spessart through Gelnhausen to join the Main at Hanau. Frederick Barbarossa built his imperial palace on an island in the river at Gelnhausen.

kyiv.s: Kyiv is the capital of Ukraine, on the Dnieper river. From the late 9th century it was the capital of Kievan Rus', the first East Slavic state, whose prince Vladimir the Great accepted Christianity in 988.

kaub.s: Kaub is a small wine town on the right bank of the Rhine in Rhineland-Palatinate, in the Upper Middle Rhine Valley. The island toll castle of Pfalzgrafenstein in the river beside it collected Rhine tolls for the Electoral Palatinate, and on New Year's night 1813–1814 the…

kourou.s: Kourou is a town on the coast of French Guiana, north-west of Cayenne. It was the scene of the disastrous Kourou expedition of 1763, in which most of the thousands of French and German settlers died of disease.

kourou-expedition.s: The Kourou expedition was a French attempt in 1763–1765 to settle European colonists in French Guiana after the loss of Canada in the Seven Years' War. Some 12,000 settlers, many from Alsace and the German lands, were landed at Kourou without adequate food, shelter or…

karaikal.s: Karaikal is a coastal town on the Coromandel Coast of south-east India, in the Kaveri delta. France acquired it from the Raja of Thanjavur in 1739 and governed it as part of French India until its de facto transfer to India in 1954, completed legally in 1962.

kita-mali.s: Kita is a town in the Kayes Region of western Mali, at the foot of the Kita massif and on the Dakar–Niger Railway. French troops under Gustave Borgnis-Desbordes built a fort there in 1881, the first major post in their advance from the Senegal River to the Niger.

kitanosho-castle.s: Kitanoshō Castle was a castle in Echizen province, on the site of present-day Fukui, built from 1575 by Shibata Katsuie, a senior general of Oda Nobunaga. After Shibata's defeat by Toyotomi Hideyoshi at Shizugatake in 1583, he set the castle on fire and killed himself there…

kaibara-ekken.s: Kaibara Ekken was a Japanese Neo-Confucian scholar and botanist who served the Kuroda lords of the Fukuoka domain. He wrote widely in plain Japanese on ethics, education, health and natural history, including the Yamato honzō, a study of Japanese plants and animals, and the…

kuroda-yoshitaka.s: Kuroda Yoshitaka, better known as Kuroda Kanbei, was a Japanese samurai and strategist who served Toyotomi Hideyoshi in his campaigns to unify Japan and was rewarded with lands in Buzen province. A convert to Christianity, he later retired as the lay monk Josui.

kaundinya-i.s: Kaundinya is the legendary founder of the ruling line of Funan in the lower Mekong region. According to Chinese histories, he was a Brahmin from abroad, called Hun Tian, who arrived by ship, defeated and married the local queen Liu Ye, and became king; a later Cham inscription…

kashag.s: The Kashag was the governing council of Tibet under the Ganden Phodrang government, formally established in 1751 after reforms by the Qing and the Seventh Dalai Lama. It normally had four ministers, the kalons, usually one monk and three lay officials, who answered to the…

kharia-people.s: The Kharia are an Adivasi people of eastern India, living mainly in Jharkhand, Odisha, Chhattisgarh and West Bengal. They speak Kharia, a Munda language of the Austroasiatic family, and have traditionally lived by farming, forest gathering and labour.

kurukh-people.s: The Oraon, who call themselves Kurukh, are an Adivasi people of eastern and central India, living mainly in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Odisha and West Bengal. They speak Kurukh, a Dravidian language, and traditionally farmed the uplands of the Chota Nagpur plateau.

kedarnath.s: Kedarnath is a Hindu pilgrimage town in Rudraprayag district, Uttarakhand, India, near the source of the Mandakini river at about 3,580 metres. Its temple of Shiva is one of the twelve jyotirlingas and one of the Char Dham sites.

karnasuvarna.s: Karnasuvarna was the capital of King Shashanka of Gauda in the early 7th century, in present-day Murshidabad district of West Bengal, India. Its site is identified with Rajbadidanga near Chiruti, where excavations uncovered a Buddhist monastery taken to be the Raktamrittika…

kionga-triangle.s: The Kionga Triangle is a small area of land at the mouth of the Rovuma river, on the border between Tanzania and Mozambique. Germany took it from Portuguese control in 1894 as part of German East Africa, and Portuguese troops reoccupied it in 1916.

kokopo.s: Kokopo is a town on the Gazelle Peninsula of New Britain, Papua New Guinea. As Herbertshöhe it was the capital of German New Guinea from 1899 until the move to nearby Rabaul in 1910.

kpalime.s: Kpalimé is a town in south-western Togo, in hilly country near the border with Ghana. The German colonial railway from Lomé reached it in 1907 and became known as the cocoa railway because it carried cocoa and other produce from the region to the coast.

kiritimati.s: Kiritimati, also known as Christmas Island, is a large coral atoll in the Line Islands of the central Pacific and part of Kiribati. Sighted by James Cook on Christmas Eve 1777, it was annexed by Britain in 1888 and joined the Gilbert and Ellice Islands colony in 1919.

kollidam-river.s: The Kollidam, also called the Coleroon, is the northern distributary of the Kaveri river in Tamil Nadu, southern India. It branches off just above Srirangam, enclosing the island temple town between its two streams, and flows north-east to the Bay of Bengal.

kipchak-languages.s: The Kipchak languages are a branch of the Turkic languages spoken from eastern Europe to Central Asia, including Kazakh, Kyrgyz, Tatar, Bashkir, Karakalpak, Nogai and Crimean Tatar. They descend from the speech of the medieval Kipchaks and Cumans, which became the common…

kalhana.s: Kalhana was a Kashmiri Brahmin poet and historian who wrote the Rajatarangini, 'River of Kings', in Sanskrit verse in 1148–1150. Covering the kings of Kashmir from legendary times to his own day, it is the earliest Indian work to attempt a critical history, drawing on…

karkota-dynasty.s: The Karkota dynasty ruled Kashmir from about 625 to 855. Founded by Durlabhavardhana, it reached its height under Lalitaditya Muktapida in the eighth century, whose campaigns reached far into northern India and who built the Sun Temple at Martand.

kirtipur.s: Kirtipur is an old Newar town on a ridge south-west of Kathmandu, Nepal. Prithvi Narayan Shah of Gorkha failed to take it in two assaults before capturing it after a long siege in the 1760s, punishing its defenders by cutting off their noses.

kaesong.s: Kaesong is a city in southern North Korea, near the border with South Korea. As Kaegyong it was the capital of Goryeo from 919 to 1392, apart from the court's refuge on Ganghwa island from 1232 to 1270.

kragujevac-massacre.s: The Kragujevac massacre was the mass shooting of some 2,800 men and boys, including schoolboys, by German troops in the Serbian town of Kragujevac in October 1941. It was a reprisal for attacks by Partisans and Chetniks that had killed German soldiers, under an order that 100…

kars.s: Kars is a city in north-eastern Turkey, on a high plateau near the Armenian border, dominated by a medieval citadel. It was the capital of Bagratid Armenia in the tenth century and then of the small Kingdom of Kars, and later a contested Ottoman fortress, held by Russia from…

kalevala.s: The Kalevala is the Finnish national epic, compiled by Elias Lönnrot from oral folk poetry he collected in Finland and Karelia. First published in 1835 and enlarged in 1849, its poems tell of the creation of the world and of heroes such as Väinämöinen.

kestutis.s: Kęstutis was a Grand Duke of Lithuania and son of Gediminas who ruled the western lands of Lithuania from Trakai from the 1340s. For decades he shared power with his brother Algirdas, defending Lithuania against the Teutonic Order while Algirdas expanded into Rus'.

konstantin-vasilyevich-of-suzdal.s: Konstantin Vasilyevich was Prince of Suzdal and, from 1341, the first Grand Prince of Nizhny Novgorod–Suzdal, a title granted by the Golden Horde. He moved his seat from Suzdal to Nizhny Novgorod, encouraged settlement along the Volga and Oka, and rivalled Moscow,…

komi-peoples.s: The Komi are a Finno-Ugric people of north-eastern European Russia, divided mainly into the Komi-Zyrians of the Komi Republic and the Komi-Permyaks of Perm Krai. Their lands supplied furs to Novgorod and then Moscow, and in the late fourteenth century Stephen of Perm converted…

komi-permyaks.s: The Komi-Permyaks are a Finno-Ugric people of the upper Kama basin in Perm Krai, Russia, closely related to the Komi of the Komi Republic and speaking their own form of the Komi language. Their land formed the core of the medieval principality of Great Perm, and from 1925 to…

kokstad.s: Kokstad is a town in the KwaZulu-Natal province of South Africa, founded in 1869 at the foot of Mount Currie by the Griqua leader Adam Kok III and named after him. It was the capital of Griqualand East until the territory was annexed to the Cape Colony in 1879, and it remains…

khoekhoe.s: The Khoekhoe, formerly called Khoikhoi, are the indigenous pastoral peoples of south-western Africa, who herded cattle and sheep and spoke click languages. At the Cape they were the first people the Dutch met in 1652, and in the following century wars, smallpox and settler…

kyide-nyimagon.s: Kyide Nyimagon was a descendant of the royal line of the Tibetan Empire, usually considered a great-grandson of Langdarma, who moved to western Tibet in the 10th century after the empire collapsed. He established a kingdom in Ngari, and on his death his lands were divided…

kahramanmaras.s: Kahramanmaraş is a city in south-eastern Turkey, at the foot of the Taurus Mountains. In the early Iron Age it was Marqas, capital of the Neo-Hittite kingdom of Gurgum, and later, as Germanicia and then Maraş, it was a frontier town between Byzantium and the Islamic world.

kontor.s: A Kontor was a foreign trading post of the Hanseatic League, a self-governing community of German merchants with its own aldermen, statutes, treasury and court. The four main Kontore were at Novgorod (the Peterhof), Bergen (the German Wharf, or Bryggen), Bruges and London (the…

kadohadacho.s: The Kadohadacho were one of the three Caddo confederacies, living along the great bend of the Red River where Texas, Arkansas and Oklahoma meet. They traded with the French from the early 18th century.

kyushu.s: Kyushu is the third-largest of Japan's main islands, lying south-west of Honshu and closest to Korea and China. It was an early gateway for continental culture and, in the 16th century, for Portuguese traders and Christianity.

kalenga.s: Kalenga was the fortified capital of the Hehe chief Mkwawa in the southern highlands of present-day Tanzania, near Iringa. German troops stormed it in October 1894, but Mkwawa escaped and fought a guerrilla war until 1898.

kunduz.s: Kunduz is a city in northern Afghanistan, capital of Kunduz province, on the Kunduz River in the fertile plain of ancient Bactria. It was a capital of Tokharistan under the Hephthalites and the Turkic yabghus, and in the 19th century the seat of Murad Beg's Uzbek khanate of…

kavad-i.s: Kavad I was Sasanian King of Kings of Iran from 488 to 496 and again from 498 or 499 to 531. He owed his throne to Hephthalite support and, after nobles deposed him for favouring the Mazdakite movement, regained it with a Hephthalite army.

kakiali.s: Kakiali was a leader of Hitu, on the northern peninsula of Ambon Island in Maluku, who held the title of captain of Hitu. In the 1630s and early 1640s he led resistance against the Dutch East India Company and its clove monopoly, in alliance with Makassar and Ternatean rebels.

kapahaha.s: Kapahaha was a mountain stronghold on the Hitu peninsula of Ambon Island, in Maluku, Indonesia. It served as the last refuge of the Hitu resistance against the Dutch East India Company, and its capture by Dutch forces in 1646 ended the Hitu war.

kwazulu-natal.s: KwaZulu-Natal is a province on the east coast of South Africa, created in 1994 by merging the province of Natal with the KwaZulu homeland. Its largest city is Durban and its capital Pietermaritzburg.

kowloon.s: Kowloon is an urban area of Hong Kong on the peninsula facing Hong Kong Island across Victoria Harbour. Its southern tip was ceded to Britain by China in 1860 under the Convention of Peking, and the lands to the north were leased in 1898 as part of the New Territories.

kabars.s: The Kabars were three tribes that rebelled against the Khazar Khaganate in the 9th century and joined the Hungarians. According to Constantine VII, they formed the vanguard in war and taught the Hungarians the Khazar language.

karakoram-highway.s: The Karakoram Highway is a road that runs from Hasan Abdal in northern Pakistan through the Karakoram range and over the Khunjerab Pass to Kashgar in Xinjiang, China. Built by Pakistan and China between 1959 and 1979, it is one of the highest paved roads in the world.

koka-shiga.s: Kōka is a district and city in the south of Shiga Prefecture, Japan, neighbouring the old province of Iga. In the Sengoku period it was governed by a league of local warrior families and, like Iga, was famous for its ninja.

kogi-state.s: Kogi State is a state in central Nigeria, created in 1991, with Lokoja as its capital. It lies at the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers.

kaskaskia.s: The Kaskaskia were one of the main peoples of the Illinois Confederation, an Algonquian-speaking alliance of the upper Mississippi valley. In 1673 their Grand Village on the Illinois river near Starved Rock was visited by Marquette and Jolliet.

kwara-state.s: Kwara State is a state in western central Nigeria, created in 1967, with its capital at Ilorin. It lies where the Yoruba south-west meets the north, and much of it was once ruled by the Ilorin Emirate, founded in the 1820s as part of the Sokoto Caliphate.

kakegawa-castle.s: Kakegawa Castle is a Japanese castle in Kakegawa, Shizuoka Prefecture, in the former province of Tōtōmi. Built in the early 16th century by a retainer of the Imagawa clan, it was where Imagawa Ujizane held out against Tokugawa Ieyasu before surrendering in 1569.

kaisheim.s: Kaisheim is a market town in the Donau-Ries district of Swabia, Bavaria, north of Donauwörth. It grew around a Cistercian abbey founded in 1133, which became an imperial abbey and built a large baroque complex with a library and an imperial hall, the Kaisersaal.

kornelimunster.s: Kornelimünster is a district of Aachen in western Germany that grew around a Benedictine abbey founded in 814 by Louis the Pious for Benedict of Aniane, at a place then called Inda. The abbey took its new name from relics of Pope Cornelius received in 875, and its abbots ruled…

kurt-hahn.s: Kurt Hahn was a German-born educator. Secretary and adviser to Prince Maximilian of Baden, he founded the Schule Schloss Salem boarding school with him in 1920.

kabaka-of-buganda.s: The Kabaka of Buganda is the title of the king of Buganda, the largest of the traditional kingdoms in present-day Uganda. The Kabaka ruled through appointed chiefs and a council, the Lukiiko, and in the 19th century dealt with Arab traders, Christian missionaries and the British.

kennyo.s: Kennyo was the eleventh head priest of the Hongan-ji, the main temple of the Jodo Shinshu Buddhist school, from 1554. From the fortified temple of Ishiyama Hongan-ji in Osaka he led the Ikko-ikki leagues in a long war against Oda Nobunaga from 1570.

keban-dam.s: The Keban Dam is a hydroelectric dam on the Euphrates in eastern Turkey, completed in 1974 near Elazığ. It was the first of the large dams on the upper Euphrates and created one of Turkey's largest reservoirs.

katarabumi.s: Katarabumi was a sultan of Jailolo on Halmahera in the Maluku Islands in the mid-16th century. He made Jailolo a rival of neighbouring Ternate, but Ternate and its Portuguese allies attacked the kingdom repeatedly, and in 1551 he was forced to submit.

kathiawar.s: Kathiawar, also called Saurashtra, is a large peninsula of western India in the state of Gujarat, bounded by the Gulf of Kutch and the Gulf of Khambhat. Named after the Kathi people, it was divided in the colonial period among some two hundred princely states supervised by the…

kalijati.s: Kalijati is an airfield in Subang regency, West Java, Indonesia. On 8 March 1942 the Dutch colonial authorities met the Japanese commander Hitoshi Imamura there and agreed to the capitulation of the Royal Netherlands East Indies Army, ending Dutch rule over the colony until…

kathi-people.s: The Kathi are a community of the Kathiawar peninsula in Gujarat, India, which is named after them. Pastoralists and warriors who are thought to have entered the region from the north in the medieval period, they founded several small states, including Jasdan, Jetpur and Bilkha.

khaspur.s: Khaspur is a historic site in the Cachar district of southern Assam, India, near Silchar, which was the last capital of the Kachari kingdom from the 18th century. Ruins of the royal palace, including gateways and temples, survive from the time of the Dimasa kings.

kakusthavarma.s: Kakusthavarma was a king of the Kadamba dynasty of Banavasi in Karnataka in the 5th century, regarded as one of its most powerful rulers. The Talagunda inscription records that he married his daughters into royal houses, including, according to later readings, the Gupta and…

kenroku-en.s: Kenroku-en is a landscape garden in Kanazawa, Japan, counted among the Three Great Gardens of Japan. It was developed over the 17th to 19th centuries by the Maeda lords of the Kaga domain beside Kanazawa Castle, with ponds, streams, teahouses and carefully pruned trees.

kaga-province.s: Kaga Province was an old province of Japan on the Sea of Japan coast, now the southern part of Ishikawa Prefecture. From 1488 to 1580 it was ruled by the Ikko-ikki leagues of True Pure Land believers, and contemporaries called it a province held by peasants.

kanazawa.s: Kanazawa is a city on the Sea of Japan coast of Honshu and the capital of Ishikawa Prefecture. It grew from a temple centre of the Ikko-ikki founded in 1546 into the castle town of the Maeda lords of Kaga, one of the largest cities of Edo-period Japan.

krishnaraja-kalachuri.s: Krishnaraja was a king of the Kalachuris of Mahishmati in western India in the mid-6th century. His silver coins, showing his head and a bull, circulated widely in Malwa, Gujarat and the northern Deccan and were imitated long after his reign.
