kartavirya-arjuna.s: Kartavirya Arjuna is a legendary king of the Haihayas in Hindu tradition, said to have ruled from Mahishmati on the Narmada and to have had a thousand arms. The Puranas tell of his victory over Ravana and of his seizure of the sage Jamadagni's cow, for which Parashurama killed…

kokalla-i.s: Kokalla I was the founder of the power of the Kalachuris of Tripuri in central India in the late 9th century. Ruling the Chedi country around Tripuri, near modern Jabalpur, he raided widely and made marriage alliances with the Rashtrakuta dynasty, giving his daughter to King…

kondh.s: The Kondh are an Adivasi people of the hills and forests of Odisha in eastern India, speaking the Dravidian languages Kui and Kuvi. They are the largest tribal community in Odisha.

khudabad.s: Khudabad is a ruined town near Dadu in Sindh, Pakistan, founded by the Kalhora dynasty in the early 18th century. It served as the Kalhora capital in the middle of the century, with a large congregational mosque whose remains still stand.

kalmar.s: Kalmar is a city on the south-east coast of Sweden, facing the island of Öland across the Kalmar Strait. Its castle guarded the medieval border with Denmark, and in 1397 Eric of Pomerania was crowned there as king of Denmark, Norway and Sweden, founding the Kalmar Union.

karorsinghia-misl.s: The Karorsinghia Misl was one of the Sikh confederacies, or misls, of 18th-century Punjab, named after its leader Karora Singh. Its chiefs seized lands south of the Sutlej and in the region of the upper Yamuna.

kanto-region.s: The Kantō region is the largest plain of Japan, in eastern Honshu, now covering Tokyo and six surrounding prefectures. Historically it comprised eight provinces and was the base of the warrior class: the Kamakura shogunate ruled from there, the Kamakura and Koga kubo governed…

koga-ibaraki.s: Koga is a city in Ibaraki Prefecture in the Kanto region of Japan, formerly in Shimousa province. In 1455 Ashikaga Shigeuji, driven from Kamakura, made it his base, and his line ruled from there as the Koga kubo until the late 16th century.

kamakura.s: Kamakura is a coastal city south of Tokyo in Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan. Minamoto no Yoritomo made it the seat of his warrior government in the 1180s, and it remained the capital of the Kamakura shogunate until 1333, when Nitta Yoshisada stormed it.

kamakhya-temple.s: The Kamakhya Temple is a Hindu temple to the mother goddess Kamakhya on Nilachal Hill in Guwahati, Assam. One of the most important centres of Shakta and Tantric worship in India, it was patronised by the kings of Kamarupa.

karatoya-river.s: The Karatoya is a river of northern Bengal, flowing through north-eastern Bangladesh. Considered sacred in Hindu tradition, it formed the ancient boundary between Kamarupa and Bengal, and the early city of Mahasthangarh, ancient Pundranagara, stood on its banks.

kangra-fort.s: Kangra Fort, historically Nagarkot, is a large hill fort near Kangra in Himachal Pradesh, India, and the seat of the Katoch rulers of Kangra. It guarded a rich temple treasury that Mahmud of Ghazni plundered in 1009.

keraton-kanoman.s: Keraton Kanoman is a royal palace in Cirebon on the north coast of West Java, Indonesia, built in the late 17th century as the seat of the sultans of Kanoman after the division of Cirebon in 1677. Decorated with Chinese and European porcelain plates and holding old royal…

kumul-rebellion.s: The Kumul Rebellion was an uprising of Uyghurs and other Muslims in Xinjiang that began at Hami, or Kumul, in 1931 after the provincial governor Jin Shuren abolished the Kumul Khanate. The rebels called in the Hui warlord Ma Zhongying, and the revolt spread across the…

korsakov-sakhalin.s: Korsakov is a port town on Aniva Bay at the southern end of Sakhalin, Russia. Founded as a Russian post in 1853, it passed to Japan in 1905 as Otomari, where the Karafuto Agency was first set up in 1907.

karakalpaks.s: The Karakalpaks are a Kipchak Turkic people living mainly in the Amu Darya delta south of the Aral Sea, in the Republic of Karakalpakstan in Uzbekistan. Their name means black hats.

karaman.s: Karaman is a city in south-central Turkey, known in Byzantine and Seljuk times as Larende. From the late 13th century it was a main seat of the Karamanid dynasty, which gave the city its modern name and built mosques and madrasas there.

karaman-bey.s: Karaman Bey was a 13th-century Turkmen chief in the Taurus Mountains of southern Anatolia, from whom the Karamanid dynasty and its beylik took their name. The son of Nure Sufi, he served and at times opposed the Seljuk sultans of Rum, who recognised his hold on lands around…

kantarawaddy.s: Kantarawaddy was the largest of the Karenni States in the hills of eastern Burma, ruled by a hereditary chief with the Shan title of saopha. Britain and the Burmese king recognised the independence of the Karenni states in 1875, and in 1892 their chiefs accepted British…

kyebogyi.s: Kyebogyi was one of the Karenni States in the hills of eastern Burma, a small chiefdom ruled by a hereditary saopha. Like Kantarawaddy and Bawlake, it was recognised as independent by Britain and the Burmese king in 1875 and became a British feudatory in 1892.

kayah-state.s: Kayah State is the smallest state of Myanmar, in the hills of the east bordering Thailand, with its capital at Loikaw. It was formed from the former Karenni States, which joined the Union of Burma in 1948, and was renamed Kayah State in 1952.

karenni-people.s: The Karenni, also called the Red Karen or Kayah, are a Karen people of the hills of eastern Myanmar, living mainly in Kayah State and across the border in Thailand. In the 19th century their chiefs ruled several small states that Britain and Burma recognised as independent in…

keraton-kasepuhan.s: Keraton Kasepuhan is the palace of the Sultan Sepuh in Cirebon on the north coast of West Java, Indonesia. It grew from the older Pakungwati court of Cirebon's rulers and became the seat of the senior sultanate after Cirebon was divided in 1677.

kashmiri-pandits.s: The Kashmiri Pandits are the Hindu Brahmin community of the Kashmir valley, long prominent as scholars, scribes and administrators. They served successive rulers, from the Hindu kings to the sultans, Mughals, Afghans, Sikhs and Dogras.

kadashman-enlil-i.s: Kadashman-Enlil I was a Kassite king of Babylonia in the 14th century BCE. Letters in the Amarna archive record his exchanges with the pharaoh Amenhotep III, including his sister's marriage to the pharaoh and disputes over gifts of gold and the treatment of Babylonian princesses.

kurigalzu-i.s: Kurigalzu I was a Kassite king of Babylonia in the early 14th century BCE. He built extensively in the old cities of Babylonia and founded a new royal city, Dur-Kurigalzu, with a ziggurat near modern Baghdad.

kumaon.s: Kumaon is the eastern of the two divisions of Uttarakhand in the central Himalaya of India, with Nainital and Almora as its main towns. It was ruled by the Katyuri kings and then for centuries by the Chand dynasty from Champawat and Almora.

kabirdham-district.s: Kabirdham district is a district of Chhattisgarh, India, with its headquarters at Kawardha. Formed in 1998 as Kawardha district and renamed in 2003, it covers the former princely state of Kawardha and the forested slopes of the Maikal range.

kazakh-famine-of-1930-1933.s: The Kazakh famine of 1930–1933, known in Kazakh as the Asharshylyk, was a man-made famine in Soviet Kazakhstan. Forced collectivisation, the settlement of nomads and heavy requisitioning of grain and livestock destroyed herds that most Kazakhs depended on.

kyzylorda.s: Kyzylorda is a city on the Syr Darya in southern Kazakhstan. It grew from the Kokand fortress of Ak-Mechet, taken by Russia in 1853 and renamed Perovsk.

kenesary-kasymov.s: Kenesary Kasymov was a Kazakh sultan, grandson of Ablai Khan, who led the largest Kazakh uprising against Russian rule, from 1837 to 1847. He was proclaimed khan in 1841 and tried to restore the khanate, but Russian forces pushed him south.

karlag.s: Karlag, the Karaganda Corrective Labour Camp, was one of the largest camps of the Soviet Gulag, on the steppe of central Kazakhstan. From 1931 to 1959 its prisoners worked mainly on vast farms supplying the Karaganda coal-mining region.

koreans.s: The Koreans are the people of the Korean Peninsula, divided since 1945 between North and South Korea, with large communities in China, Japan, the former Soviet Union and the United States. Japan ruled Korea from 1910 to 1945 and moved many Koreans as labourers.

kashagan-field.s: The Kashagan Field is a large offshore oil field in the shallow northern Caspian Sea off western Kazakhstan, discovered in 2000. Developed by an international consortium, it was among the largest oil discoveries of recent decades.

kumukh.s: Kumukh is a large mountain village in the Lak district of Dagestan, Russia, the historic centre of the Lak people. One of the earliest centres of Islam in mountainous Dagestan, it was the seat of the Kazikumukh shamkhals and, from the 17th century, of the khans of Kazikumukh.

kumyks.s: The Kumyks are a Turkic people of Dagestan in the North Caucasus, living mainly on the plain between the mountains and the Caspian Sea. They formed the core of the Shamkhalate of Tarki and other principalities, and Kumyk served as a common language of trade across the region.

kedah-river.s: The Kedah River is a river of north-western Peninsular Malaysia that flows through Alor Setar to the Strait of Malacca at Kuala Kedah. Its lower course runs through the rice plains of Kedah, the main rice-growing region of Malaysia.

kertajaya.s: Kertajaya was the last king of the Kediri Kingdom in East Java. According to the Pararaton he quarrelled with the Hindu and Buddhist clergy, who turned to Ken Arok, ruler of Tumapel.

kakawin-bharatayuddha.s: The Kakawin Bharatayuddha is an Old Javanese poem retelling the great war of the Mahabharata, completed in 1157 under King Jayabaya of Kediri. It was begun by the poet Mpu Sedah and finished by Mpu Panuluh.

kidal.s: Kidal is a town in north-eastern Mali, in the Adrar des Ifoghas mountains of the Sahara. It is the main centre of the Kel Adagh Tuareg and was founded as a French post in the early 20th century.

keladi.s: Keladi is a village in the Shimoga district of Karnataka, India, in the Malnad hills near Sagar. It was the original seat of the Keladi Nayakas, local chiefs who served the Vijayanagara Empire from about 1499 and later ruled the region independently from Ikkeri and Bidanur.

kaocen-ag-mohammed.s: Kaocen ag Mohammed was a Tuareg leader of the Kel Ewey from the Aïr in present-day Niger. Linked to the Sanusi order, he led a major revolt against French rule in 1916–1917 and besieged the French garrison of Agadez for several months.

kusunoki-masashige.s: Kusunoki Masashige was a Japanese warrior who fought for Emperor Go-Daigo in the overthrow of the Kamakura shogunate in 1333. When Ashikaga Takauji turned against the emperor, Masashige was defeated and killed at the Battle of Minatogawa in 1336.

kenya-african-national-union.s: The Kenya African National Union (KANU) is a Kenyan political party founded in 1960 and led by Jomo Kenyatta, which took the country to independence in 1963. It ruled Kenya without interruption for almost four decades, becoming the sole legal party under Daniel arap Moi in 1982.

kendujhar.s: Kendujhar, also known as Keonjhar or Keonjhargarh, is a town in northern Odisha, India, the headquarters of Kendujhar district. It was the capital of the princely state of Keonjhar until it merged with Odisha in 1948.

karthaia.s: Karthaia was one of the four ancient cities of the island of Keos in the Cyclades, on its south-east coast. Its ruins include temples of Apollo and Athena, a theatre and city walls.

koressia.s: Koressia was one of the four ancient cities of the island of Keos in the Cyclades, at the main harbour on the north-west coast. In the 3rd century BCE it became a Ptolemaic naval base renamed Arsinoe.

kot-diji.s: Kot Diji is a site in Khairpur District of Sindh, Pakistan, south of the city of Khairpur. Its archaeological mound gives its name to the Kot Diji culture, an early Harappan phase of the early 3rd millennium BCE that preceded the mature Indus Valley Civilisation.

kherlen-river.s: The Kherlen is a river of eastern Mongolia and north-eastern China, about 1,250 kilometres long, which rises in the Khentii Mountains and flows east into Hulun Lake. Its valley, with that of the Onon, was the homeland of Genghis Khan's Mongols, and an early Mongol royal camp…

kazan.s: Kazan is a city on the Volga at its confluence with the Kazanka, the capital of the Republic of Tatarstan in Russia. Founded as a Bulgar fortress, it became the capital of the Khanate of Kazan in the 15th century and was stormed by Ivan IV in 1552, a victory commemorated by St…

khoy.s: Khoy is a city in West Azerbaijan province in north-western Iran, north of Lake Urmia and near the Turkish border. It lay on the trade route between Tabriz and Anatolia, and the Battle of Chaldiran was fought north-west of it in 1514.

khudayar-khan.s: Khudayar Khan was khan of Kokand, holding the throne three times between 1845 and 1875 amid civil wars between settled and nomadic factions. Having lost Tashkent and much territory to Russia, he became its dependant, and his heavy taxes provoked a revolt in 1875 that drove him…

khanty.s: The Khanty, formerly called Ostyaks, are a Finno-Ugric people of western Siberia, living mainly along the Ob and Irtysh and their tributaries in the Khanty-Mansi Autonomous Okrug. Traditionally hunters, fishers and reindeer herders, they paid fur tribute to the Khanate of…

kuchum.s: Kuchum was the last khan of Sibir, a Shibanid descendant of Genghis Khan who seized power from the Taibugid ruler Yadegar in 1563. He stopped the fur tribute paid to Ivan IV and promoted Islam among his subjects.

khandesh.s: Khandesh is a historical region in the valley of the Tapti river in north-western Maharashtra, India, now mainly covered by the Jalgaon, Dhule and Nandurbar districts. From the late 14th century to 1601 it was ruled by the Faruqi sultans from Burhanpur.

karkheh-river.s: The Karkheh is a river of western Iran, about 900 kilometres long, which rises in the Zagros Mountains and flows south through Lorestan and Khuzestan, passing near the ruins of Susa, to the Hawizeh Marshes on the Iraqi border. Identified with the ancient Choaspes, it watered…

khorramabad.s: Khorramabad is the capital of Lorestan province in western Iran, in a valley of the Zagros Mountains. Prehistoric caves nearby show very long settlement, and the town grew around the citadel of Falak-ol-Aflak.

kiche-people.s: The K'iche' are a Maya people of the western highlands of Guatemala, centred on the departments of El Quiché, Totonicapán and Quetzaltenango. In the 15th century their kingdom, ruled from Q'umarkaj, dominated much of the highlands until Pedro de Alvarado conquered it in 1524.

kiqab.s: K'iq'ab was a K'iche' Maya king of the mid-15th century, under whom the kingdom ruled from Q'umarkaj reached its greatest extent across western Guatemala and the Pacific slope. Late in his reign a revolt by his sons and lords weakened his authority, and around 1470 the…

kidara.s: Kidara was the founder of the Kidarite kingdom, who ruled Bactria and later Gandhara around the late 4th and early 5th centuries CE. Known mainly from coins, which bear his name and copy Kushan and Sasanian designs, he claimed the old Kushan royal title and gave his name to…

kumano.s: Kumano is a mountainous, forested region in the south of the Kii Peninsula of Japan, in Wakayama, Mie and Nara prefectures. It is famous for the Three Grand Shrines of Kumano, at Hongū, Shingū and Nachi, which drew emperors and commoners along the pilgrimage routes of the…

kyoho-reforms.s: The Kyōhō reforms were measures introduced by the eighth Tokugawa shogun, Yoshimune, named after the Kyōhō era of 1716–1736, to restore the shogunate's finances and discipline. They included higher rice taxes, encouragement of new farmland, sumptuary laws, a petition box for…

kilwa-chronicle.s: The Kilwa Chronicle is a history of the Kilwa Sultanate on the Swahili coast of East Africa, surviving in an Arabic version written in the early 16th century and a Portuguese summary by João de Barros. It traces the dynasty to Ali ibn al-Hasan, said to be a prince from Shiraz…

kilwa-kisiwani.s: Kilwa Kisiwani is an island off the southern coast of Tanzania, seat of the Kilwa Sultanate, which from the 13th century controlled the gold trade from Sofala. Ibn Battuta visited in 1331 and praised it as one of the most beautiful towns in the world.

kipchaks.s: The Kipchaks were a Turkic nomadic people who formed the western wing of the Kimek confederation on the Irtysh and from the 11th century spread across the steppe from Kazakhstan to the Black Sea, where they were known as Cumans or Polovtsians. The Mongols broke their power in…

kuria-kiribati.s: Kuria is an atoll of two islands in the central Gilbert Islands of Kiribati, west of Aranuka and Abemama. In the 19th century Tem Baiteke of Abemama conquered it with firearms acquired from traders, and it remained part of the Abemama kingdom until Britain declared a…

kiribati.s: Kiribati is an island republic in the central Pacific Ocean, made up of 33 atolls and reef islands in the Gilbert, Phoenix and Line groups, with its capital at South Tarawa. The Gilbert Islands became a British protectorate in 1892 and later part of the Gilbert and Ellice…

kutaisi.s: Kutaisi is a city on the Rioni river in western Georgia. In the late 8th century it became the capital of the Kingdom of Abkhazia, and it remained a royal seat of united Georgia until David IV took Tbilisi in 1122.

kincora.s: Kincora, Cenn Corad in Irish, was the royal residence of Brian Boru and the kings of the Dál gCais and Uí Briain, at Killaloe in County Clare on the River Shannon. Brian ruled from it as king of Munster and high king of Ireland until his death in 1014.

kabyles.s: The Kabyles are a Berber people of Kabylia in northern Algeria, a mountainous region east of Algiers that includes the Djurdjura range. Speaking the Kabyle language, they lived in dense village communities governed by assemblies and long kept their autonomy from Ottoman Algiers.

kusaila.s: Kusaila was a Christian Berber chief of the Awraba confederation who led resistance to the Arab conquest of North Africa in the 680s. Won over and converted by Abu al-Muhajir Dinar, he was later humiliated by Uqba ibn Nafi, whom he ambushed and killed near Biskra in 682 or 683.

kirkuk.s: Kirkuk is a city in northern Iraq, east of the Tigris, on the site of ancient Arrapha, capital of a Hurrian kingdom in the 15th and 14th centuries BCE. Its citadel mound has been occupied for millennia.

kintamani.s: Kintamani is a highland district of Bangli Regency in Bali, Indonesia, on the rim of the great caldera of Mount Batur. Overlooking the active volcano and Lake Batur, it is home to old mountain villages and temples, among them Pura Ulun Danu Batur, dedicated to the goddess of…

kubuna-confederacy.s: Kubuna is one of the three traditional confederacies of Fiji, together with Burebasaga and Tovata. Headed by the Vunivalu of Bau, it is centred on the small island of Bau and the adjacent coast of Viti Levu.

kutna-hora.s: Kutná Hora is a town in Central Bohemia, Czech Republic, which grew rich from silver mines opened in the late 13th century. Around 1300 Wenceslaus II set up a royal mint there to strike the Prague groschen, and the town became one of the wealthiest in Bohemia, second only to…

knowth.s: Knowth is a Neolithic passage tomb complex in the Boyne valley, County Meath, Ireland, built around 3200 BCE and part of the Brú na Bóinne World Heritage Site. Its great mound covers two passage tombs and is ringed by smaller satellite tombs, and it holds the largest…

kampala.s: Kampala is the capital and largest city of Uganda, near the northern shore of Lake Victoria. It grew around Mengo, the capital of the kabakas of Buganda, and the hill of Old Kampala, where Frederick Lugard built a fort for the Imperial British East Africa Company in 1890.

kintu.s: Kintu is the first man and founding hero of Buganda in Ganda tradition. Myths tell how he came to earth with a cow, married Nambi, daughter of the sky god Ggulu, and how her brother Walumbe, Death, followed them to earth.

kulango.s: The Kulango are a Gur-speaking people of north-eastern Ivory Coast and western Ghana, living around Bouna and Bondoukou. They are farmers whose villages were traditionally led by earth-priests responsible for the land and its shrines.

kabalega.s: Kabalega was omukama (king) of Bunyoro in western Uganda from 1870 to 1899. He built a standing army, the abarusura, revived Bunyoro's power, reconquered Toro in 1876 and resisted the advance of Buganda.

kibiro.s: Kibiro is a village and archaeological site on the eastern shore of Lake Albert in western Uganda, known for salt production from salt-rich soils and hot springs going back at least 700 years. Its salt was traded widely across the Great Lakes region and was an important source…

kainji-dam.s: The Kainji Dam is a hydroelectric dam on the Niger River in western Nigeria, completed in 1968. Its reservoir, Kainji Lake, flooded the old town of Bussa and other settlements, whose people were moved to new towns such as New Bussa.

kisra-borgu-tradition.s: Kisra is a legendary conqueror in the traditions of Borgu, in present-day Benin and Nigeria, said to have come from the east and to be the ancestor of the ruling dynasties of Bussa, Nikki and other Borgu kingdoms. Some scholars connect his name with Kisra, the Arabic form of…

kunjali-marakkar.s: Kunjali Marakkar was the title of the hereditary Muslim naval commanders of the Zamorin of Calicut in the 16th century. Four successive Kunjalis led fleets of fast, light vessels against the Portuguese along the Malabar Coast.

kincardineshire.s: Kincardineshire, also called the Mearns, is a historic county on the north-east coast of Scotland, between Angus and Aberdeenshire, with Stonehaven as its county town. Its fertile lowland, the Howe of the Mearns, lies south of the Mounth.

kodagu.s: Kodagu, formerly Coorg, is a hilly district of Karnataka in south-western India, in the Western Ghats, where the Kaveri river rises. Its capital is Madikeri.

kodava-people.s: The Kodavas are a people of Kodagu (Coorg) in Karnataka, south-western India, who speak the Dravidian Kodava language. Traditionally landholding farmers and warriors organised in patrilineal clans, they served in the armies of the rajas of Coorg and later in large numbers in…

keladi-nayakas.s: The Keladi Nayakas, also called the Nayakas of Ikkeri, were a dynasty that ruled the coast and western hills of present-day Karnataka from about 1499 to 1763, first as governors under the Vijayanagara Empire and then independently. Their capitals were successively Keladi,…

knin.s: Knin is a town in the Dalmatian hinterland of Croatia, on the Krka river, beneath a large hilltop fortress. It was one of the royal seats of the medieval Croatian kings and the seat of a bishop.

karlovac.s: Karlovac is a city in central Croatia, at the meeting of the Kupa, Korana, Mrežnica and Dobra rivers. It was founded in 1579 by Archduke Charles of Austria as a star-shaped fortress of the Military Frontier against the Ottomans and named after him.

karoly-khuen-hedervary.s: Károly Khuen-Héderváry was a Hungarian politician who served as ban of Croatia-Slavonia from 1883 to 1903 and twice as prime minister of Hungary. As ban he governed in an authoritarian way in the Hungarian interest and played Croatia's Serbs against the Croats to keep the…

killke-culture.s: The Killke culture is the archaeological culture of the Cusco region of Peru from about 1000 to 1400 CE, named after a distinctive style of pottery. It covers the period when the early Inca polity was forming in the Cusco valley, and its remains include early construction at…

kurunegala.s: Kurunegala is a city in the North Western Province of Sri Lanka, set among large rock outcrops, among them Elephant Rock. It served as a royal capital of the Sinhalese kings for about half a century from the late 13th century, until the court moved to Gampola around 1341.

kusugu-well.s: The Kusugu well is a historic well in Daura, in Katsina State, northern Nigeria, at the centre of the Bayajidda legend. Tradition says the stranger Bayajidda killed the snake that guarded the well and kept the people from drawing water except on Fridays, and then married Queen…

kham.s: Kham is a historical region of eastern Tibet, now divided mainly between the Tibet Autonomous Region and the Chinese provinces of Sichuan, Qinghai and Yunnan. A land of deep river gorges along the upper Yangtze, Mekong and Salween, it was long split among local kingdoms and…

komenda.s: Komenda is a coastal town in the Central Region of Ghana, west of Elmina. In the 17th century it was the port of the Akan kingdom of Eguafo, and both the English Royal African Company and the Dutch West India Company built forts there.

komenda-wars.s: The Komenda Wars were a series of conflicts from 1694 to 1700 on the Gold Coast, centred on the Akan kingdom of Eguafo and its port of Komenda. The Dutch West India Company and the English Royal African Company backed rival local rulers and allies, including the merchant John…

kamnaskires-i.s: Kamnaskires I was a local ruler of Elymais in south-western Iran who around 147 BCE took advantage of Seleucid weakness to seize Susa and issue coins as king. His successors, several of whom also bore the name Kamnaskires, ruled Elymais as a kingdom, often under Parthian…

kitab-ghanja.s: The Kitab Ghanja is an Arabic chronicle of the kingdom of Gonja in northern Ghana, compiled by Muslim scholars in the 18th century. It records the conquests of Ndewura Jakpa and the history of Gonja's rulers, and is one of the oldest written histories of the Volta region.

kofi-adinkra.s: Kofi Adinkra was king of Gyaman, the Abron kingdom around Bondoukou, in the early 19th century. He revolted against the overlordship of the Asante Empire and was defeated and killed by the Asante army in 1818.

kalocsa.s: Kalocsa is a town in southern Hungary on the plain east of the Danube. King Stephen I made it the seat of an archbishopric in the early 11th century, alongside Esztergom, and its archbishops headed the church across much of southern Hungary.

kremnica.s: Kremnica is a mining town in central Slovakia, called Körmöcbánya in the medieval Kingdom of Hungary. Its gold mines made it one of the richest towns in the kingdom, and the mint founded there in 1328 struck the Hungarian gold florin and later ducats.

kalman-tisza.s: Kálmán Tisza was prime minister of Hungary from 1875 to 1890, the longest tenure under the Dual Monarchy. He formed the Liberal Party in 1875 by merging his own party with Ferenc Deák's, accepted the Compromise of 1867 and built a political machine based on patronage and a…

killarney.s: Killarney is a town in County Kerry in south-west Ireland, beside Lough Leane and the lakes and mountains of Killarney National Park. The surrounding district was the early medieval centre of the Eóganacht Locha Léin kings of Iarmumu, with the monastery of Inisfallen and later…

klemens-von-metternich.s: Prince Klemens von Metternich was Austrian foreign minister from 1809 and chancellor from 1821 until 1848. A leading figure at the Congress of Vienna in 1814–1815, he shaped a conservative European order based on the balance of power and cooperation among monarchies.

khas-people.s: The Khas are an Indo-Aryan people of the western and central Himalayas, the original speakers of the language that became Nepali, once called Khas kura. In the Middle Ages their Khasa Malla kingdom ruled western Nepal from Sinja near Jumla, and Khas soldiers later formed much…

kafa-zone.s: Kafa Zone is an administrative zone of south-western Ethiopia, with its capital at Bonga. It covers much of the territory of the former Kingdom of Kaffa, conquered by Menelik II in 1897, and its montane forests are home to wild Arabica coffee, from whose name the word 'coffee'…

ketevan-the-martyr.s: Ketevan, known as Saint Ketevan the Martyr, was a queen of Kakheti in eastern Georgia and the mother of King Teimuraz I. Sent to Iran as a hostage, she was held for years at Shiraz and, after refusing to give up Christianity, was tortured to death on the orders of Shah Abbas I…

kandy.s: Kandy is a city in the central highlands of Sri Lanka, beside an artificial lake. It was the capital of the Kingdom of Kandy, the last independent Sinhalese kingdom, from the late 15th century until the British took it in 1815.

kandyan-convention.s: The Kandyan Convention was the agreement signed on 2 March 1815 between the British and the chiefs of the Kingdom of Kandy, after they had helped the British depose King Sri Vikrama Rajasinha. It transferred sovereignty over Kandy to the British Crown, making the whole of…

kirti-sri-rajasinha.s: Kirti Sri Rajasinha was king of Kandy from 1747 to 1782, of the Nayak dynasty of south Indian origin. A patron of Buddhism, he invited monks from Siam in 1753 to restore the higher ordination, founding the Siyam Nikaya, and restored many temples.

kamabolon.s: The Kamabolon is a sacred house at Kangaba in southern Mali, associated with the Keita clan, the royal lineage of the Mali Empire. Every seven years its thatched roof is ceremonially replaced in a festival at which griots recite the history of the Mande, including the epic of…

kabompo-river.s: The Kabompo is a river of north-western Zambia, a major tributary of the upper Zambezi. It rises near the watershed with the Congo basin and flows south-west through woodland to join the Zambezi.

kalakaua.s: Kalākaua was king of Hawaii from 1874 to 1891. He secured the Reciprocity Treaty of 1875, which let Hawaiian sugar into the United States duty-free, became the first reigning monarch to travel around the world in 1881 and revived Hawaiian traditions such as the hula.

kumari-goddess.s: Kumari is the tradition in Nepal of worshipping a young girl before puberty as the living embodiment of the goddess Taleju, a form of Durga. Chosen from the Newar Shakya caste, the Royal Kumari of Kathmandu lives in the Kumari Ghar beside Hanuman Dhoka and appears in public at…

kagera-river.s: The Kagera River is the largest river flowing into Lake Victoria, and its headwaters are often counted as the most distant source of the Nile. Rising in the highlands of Rwanda and Burundi, it forms parts of the borders of Rwanda, Burundi, Tanzania and Uganda before entering…

kagera-region.s: Kagera Region is an administrative region of north-western Tanzania, bordering Uganda, Rwanda and Burundi, with Lake Victoria to the east and its capital at Bukoba. Named after the Kagera River, it is the homeland of the Haya people, whose small kingdoms such as Kyamutwara,…

katanga.s: Katanga is a region in the south-east of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, rich in copper, cobalt and uranium. In the 19th century it was dominated by Msiri's Yeke kingdom, and from 1891 it was occupied by the Congo Free State, later becoming the mining heartland of the…

khassonke.s: The Khassonke are a people of the Kayes region of western Mali, living along the upper Senegal River. They descend from Fula herders who settled among Malinke farmers and adopted much of their culture, and their language, Khassonke, is a Mande language close to Malinke.

kunlun-mountains.s: The Kunlun Mountains are one of the longest mountain systems in Asia, stretching about 3,000 km from the Pamirs into central China along the northern edge of the Tibetan Plateau. Rivers fed by their glaciers, such as the Yurungkash and Karakash, water the oases on the southern…

koy-krylgan-kala.s: Koy-Krylgan-Kala is an ancient circular monument in Karakalpakstan, north-western Uzbekistan, built in the 4th century BCE in the Kingdom of Khwarazm. Its round central building, surrounded by a fortified ring, is thought to have served as a temple, a royal tomb and an…

kertha-gosa.s: The Kertha Gosa is an 18th-century pavilion in Semarapura, Bali, part of the palace of the Dewa Agung of Klungkung, where the court sat in judgement. Its ceilings are covered with paintings in the traditional Kamasan style showing scenes of heaven, hell and punishment from…

kimpa-vita.s: Kimpa Vita, baptised Beatriz, was a Kongolese prophet who founded the Antonian movement during the Kongo civil wars. In 1704 she claimed to be possessed by Saint Anthony, taught that Christ and the saints were Kongolese, and called for the kingdom to be reunited under a king…

kouris-river.s: The Kouris is one of the main rivers of Cyprus, rising in the Troodos Mountains and flowing south to the sea near Episkopi, west of Limassol. Ancient Kourion stood on the cliffs near its mouth and ruled the fertile land along its valley.

kizil-caves.s: The Kizil Caves are a complex of more than 230 Buddhist rock-cut caves near Kucha in Xinjiang, China, carved into cliffs above the Muzat River between about the 3rd and 8th centuries. Their wall paintings of the Buddha's lives, Jataka tales and donors are the finest surviving…

kumarajiva.s: Kumarajiva was a Buddhist monk and translator from the oasis kingdom of Kucha, the son of an Indian father and a Kuchean princess. Captured by the general Lü Guang in 384, he spent years at Guzang before Yao Xing of Later Qin brought him to Chang'an in 401.

kullu-dussehra.s: Kullu Dussehra is a week-long festival held each autumn on the Dhalpur maidan at Kullu, Himachal Pradesh, beginning on Vijayadashami. Hundreds of village deities are carried in palanquins to pay homage to Raghunath, the presiding god of the former Kullu kingdom, whose chariot…

kullu.s: Kullu is a town and district in Himachal Pradesh, India, in the valley of the Beas River. Formerly called Sultanpur, the town became the capital of the Kullu kingdom in the 17th century, when Raja Jagat Singh installed the image of Raghunath there, and it hosts the annual…

kudungga.s: Kudungga is the earliest known ruler of Kutai in eastern Borneo, named in the Sanskrit yupa inscriptions of his grandson Mulavarman from around 400. His name appears to be Indigenous rather than Indian, and the inscriptions credit his son Asvavarman, not him, with founding the…

kosoko.s: Kosoko was Oba of Lagos from 1845 to 1851. He seized the throne from his uncle Akitoye and protected the Atlantic slave trade, which brought Lagos great profit.

krishna-mandir-patan.s: The Krishna Mandir is a stone temple on Patan Durbar Square in Lalitpur, Nepal, completed in 1637 by King Siddhi Narasimha Malla. Built in the shikhara style of northern India rather than the tiered Newar style, it has carved friezes of scenes from the Mahabharata and the…

kildare.s: Kildare is a town in County Kildare, Ireland, that grew around the monastery founded by St Brigid in the late 5th or early 6th century. A double monastery of nuns and monks, it became one of the leading churches of Ireland and was closely tied to the kings of Leinster.

khosrovanuysh.s: Khosrovanuysh was an Armenian queen of the 10th century, wife of King Ashot III of Bagratid Armenia. She is credited with founding the monasteries of Sanahin, around 966, and Haghpat, around 976, in northern Armenia.

kiurikian-dynasty.s: The Kiurikian dynasty was a branch of the Armenian Bagratids that ruled the Kingdom of Lori, or Tashir-Dzoraget, in northern Armenia from around 979. Its founder Gurgen, son of Ashot III, was known as Kiurike, a Georgian form of his name.

khmu-people.s: The Khmu are an Austroasiatic-speaking people of northern Laos and neighbouring parts of Vietnam, Thailand and China. Regarded as among the earliest inhabitants of the region, they were long subordinate to the Lao kingdoms, and they had a ritual role at the royal court of…

kingkitsarath.s: Kingkitsarath was the first king of Luang Prabang, a grandson of King Sourigna Vongsa of Lan Xang. After succession disputes divided Lan Xang, he established himself at Luang Prabang in 1707 with support from Sipsongpanna, creating a kingdom separate from Vientiane.

kwango-river.s: The Kwango is a river of central Africa, about 1,100 kilometres long, that rises in the highlands of north-eastern Angola and flows north, forming part of the border with the Democratic Republic of the Congo, before joining the Kasai. Its valley was home to the kingdoms of…

kali-gandaki-river.s: The Kali Gandaki is a river of Nepal that rises near the Tibetan border in Mustang and flows south between the Dhaulagiri and Annapurna massifs through one of the deepest gorges in the world. Its valley was an old trade route between Tibet and India for salt and grain.

kabasa.s: Kabasa was the royal capital of the Kingdom of Ndongo in present-day Angola, on the plateau between the Lukala and Kwanza rivers. A Portuguese embassy under Paulo Dias de Novais reached it in 1560.

kwanza-river.s: The Kwanza is a river of Angola, about 960 kilometres long, that rises in the central highlands and flows north and west to the Atlantic south of Luanda. From the 16th century it was the main route of Portuguese expansion inland, with forts such as Massangano and Cambambe…

kigezi.s: Kigezi is a highland region of south-western Uganda, bordering Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, centred on the town of Kabale. The British created Kigezi District after the Anglo-German-Belgian boundary settlement of 1910–11, dividing lands of the former…

kumbo.s: Kumbo is a town in the North-West Region of Cameroon and the capital of the Nso kingdom, whose Fon has his palace there. It became the seat of Nso after several moves of the capital and was occupied by German forces in the first years of the 20th century.

kunene-river.s: The Kunene, or Cunene, is a river of south-western Africa that rises in the Angolan highlands and flows south and then west to the Atlantic, forming part of the border between Angola and Namibia. Its floodplains supported the Ovambo and Nkhumbi kingdoms.

kouklia.s: Kouklia is a village in the Paphos District of south-western Cyprus, built on the site of Palaepaphos, Old Paphos, the capital of one of the ancient city-kingdoms of the island. Its sanctuary of Aphrodite was one of the most famous in the Greek world.

kor-river.s: The Kor, or Kur, is a river in Fars Province in south-western Iran, about 280 km long, which flows past the plain of Marvdasht to the salt lake of Bakhtegan. Its waters, joined by the Pulvar, irrigated the heartland of Persis around Persepolis and Istakhr.

karl-august-von-hardenberg.s: Karl August von Hardenberg was a Prussian statesman who served as state chancellor from 1810 until his death in 1822. Continuing the reforms begun by Stein after Prussia's defeat in 1806, he introduced freedom of trade, emancipated the Jews in 1812 and reformed taxation and…

kano-chronicle.s: The Kano Chronicle is a history of the rulers of Kano in northern Nigeria, written in Arabic in the late 19th century from older traditions and records. It lists the kings of Kano from Bagauda, traditionally around 999, to the late 19th century, recording wars, the arrival of…

kano-state.s: Kano State is a state in north-western Nigeria, created in 1967, with its capital at the city of Kano. It is one of the most populous states of Nigeria and is mainly Hausa and Muslim.

kataragama.s: Kataragama is a pilgrimage town in south-eastern Sri Lanka, in Monaragala District, within the lands of the ancient kingdom of Ruhuna. Its shrine to the war god Skanda, known to Tamils as Murugan, is visited by Buddhists, Hindus, Muslims and Vedda people alike.

kavan-tissa.s: Kavan Tissa was a king of Ruhuna in south-eastern Sri Lanka in the 2nd century BCE, known from the Mahavamsa chronicle. Ruling from Mahagama, he strengthened the southern kingdom and married Viharamahadevi.

kinyarwanda.s: Kinyarwanda is the Bantu language of Rwanda, spoken by nearly the whole population and closely related to Kirundi of Burundi. In the precolonial kingdom it was shared by Hutu, Tutsi and Twa alike, and the royal court cultivated a rich tradition of dynastic poetry and oral…

kahone.s: Kahone is a town in west-central Senegal, just east of Kaolack on the Saloum river. It was the royal capital of the Serer kingdom of Saloum from the late 15th century, where the Buur Saloum held court with the great titled chiefs.

kaolack.s: Kaolack is a city in west-central Senegal on the Saloum river, capital of Kaolack Region. Founded near Kahone, the old capital of the kingdom of Saloum, it grew under French rule from the late 19th century into the country's main centre of the groundnut trade, served by rail…

kon-tum.s: Kon Tum is a town and province in the northern Central Highlands of Vietnam, on the Đắk Bla river. The surrounding highlands are home to the Bahnar, Sedang and other upland peoples, among whom French Catholic missionaries founded a mission in the mid-19th century.

karadordevic-dynasty.s: The Karađorđević dynasty was a Serbian royal house founded by Karađorđe Petrović, leader of the First Serbian Uprising of 1804. It alternated in power with the rival Obrenović family in the 19th century, regained the Serbian throne under Peter I after the May Coup of 1903, and…

kyustendil.s: Kyustendil is a town in western Bulgaria near the borders with Serbia and North Macedonia, known for its hot springs. As Roman Pautalia it was a flourishing spa town, and in the Middle Ages, as Velbazhd, it was a regional centre near which the Serbs defeated the Bulgarians in…

kupang.s: Kupang is the capital of the Indonesian province of East Nusa Tenggara, at the south-western end of Timor. The Dutch East India Company took the fort there in 1653, and it became the centre of Dutch power on Timor in rivalry with the Portuguese-allied Topasses of Lifau.

kapan.s: Kapan is a town in southern Armenia, the capital of Syunik Province, in the valley of the Voghji river. In the Middle Ages it was a fortress and seat of the kings of Syunik, and the area has long been known for its copper mines.

kattegat.s: The Kattegat is the sea area between the Jutland peninsula and the islands of Denmark on one side and the west coast of Sweden on the other. It links the Skagerrak and the North Sea with the Baltic through the Øresund and the Danish Belts.

khakhuli-monastery.s: Khakhuli Monastery is a medieval Georgian monastery in the historic region of Tao, today in Erzurum Province, north-eastern Turkey. It was built in the late 10th century under David III Kuropalates and became a centre of learning and manuscript copying.

klarjeti.s: Klarjeti is a historic region of south-western Georgia in the lower Chorokhi valley, today mostly in Artvin Province, Turkey. From the early 9th century it was the base of the Bagratid princes, who rebuilt Artanuji and ruled with Byzantine titles, and its monasteries became…

kaloyan-of-bulgaria.s: Kaloyan was tsar of Bulgaria from 1197 to 1207. He won recognition of his royal title from Pope Innocent III, and in 1205 he defeated the Latin crusaders at Adrianople and captured the Latin emperor Baldwin I.

killaloe.s: Killaloe is a town in County Clare, Ireland, where the River Shannon leaves Lough Derg. Nearby stood Kincora, the royal seat of Brian Boru, and the town was the centre of the O'Brien kingdom of Thomond and a bishop's see.

kaboyo-olimi-i.s: Kaboyo Olimi I was the founder of the Kingdom of Toro in western Uganda. A son of Omukama Nyamutukura Kyebambe III of Bunyoro, he rebelled around 1830 and set up an independent kingdom in the fertile lands around the Rwenzori Mountains.

kasagama-kyebambe-iv.s: Kasagama Kyebambe IV was omukama, or king, of Toro in western Uganda from 1891 to 1928. Driven out by Kabalega of Bunyoro, he was restored by Frederick Lugard of the Imperial British East Africa Company in 1891.

kongo-language.s: Kongo, or Kikongo, is a Bantu language spoken by the Kongo people in western Democratic Republic of the Congo, northern Angola and the Republic of the Congo. It was the language of the Kingdom of Kongo and its coastal neighbours Loango, Kakongo and Ngoyo.

kyauktaw.s: Kyauktaw is a town in Rakhine State, western Myanmar, on the Kaladan river north of Sittwe. The ruins of two early Arakanese capitals, Dhanyawadi and Waithali, lie nearby.

king-country.s: The King Country, in Māori Rohe Pōtae, is a region of the central North Island of New Zealand, between the Waikato and Taranaki, home mainly to Ngāti Maniapoto. After the invasion of the Waikato in 1863–1864, King Tāwhiao and his followers withdrew there, and its leaders kept…

kirata.s: Kirata is the name given in ancient Indian literature, including the Vedas, the Mahabharata and the Puranas, to peoples of the Himalaya and the hills of the north-east, often described as hunters or forest dwellers. Greek geographers also mention them.

kummanni.s: Kummanni was the chief city and religious centre of Kizzuwatna in south-eastern Anatolia in the 2nd millennium BCE, known for its temple of the goddess Hebat and its priesthood. Under the Hittite Empire it remained an important cult centre and the seat of a priest-governor.

klaipeda-revolt.s: The Klaipėda Revolt took place in January 1923, when Lithuanian irregulars, organised secretly by the Lithuanian government and presented as a local uprising, seized the Klaipėda Region from its French administration. The region had been detached from Germany by the Treaty of…

klaipeda.s: Klaipėda, historically called Memel, is Lithuania's third largest city and only seaport, at the mouth of the Curonian Lagoon on the Baltic. It grew from a castle founded by the Livonian Order in 1252 and belonged to Prussia for most of its history.

klaipeda-convention.s: The Klaipėda Convention was an international agreement signed in Paris in May 1924 between Lithuania and Britain, France, Italy and Japan. It recognised Lithuanian sovereignty over the Klaipėda Region, taken by Lithuania in the revolt of 1923, while granting the region wide…

kyotoku-war.s: The Kyōtoku War was a long conflict in the Kantō region of eastern Japan that began when the Kamakura kubo Ashikaga Shigeuji murdered the Kantō deputy Uesugi Noritada at the end of 1454. The Uesugi, backed by the shogunate, fought Shigeuji, who moved his base to Koga and…

kanmon-straits.s: The Kanmon Straits are the narrow strait between Honshu and Kyushu in Japan, linking the Inland Sea with the Sea of Japan, with Shimonoseki on the north shore and Kitakyushu on the south. The naval Battle of Dan-no-ura in 1185 was fought there, and in 1863–1864 Western…

kokura.s: Kokura is a district of Kitakyushu in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, on the southern shore of the Kanmon Straits. It grew around the castle built by Hosokawa Tadaoki from 1602 and was the castle town of the Kokura domain.

kumamoto.s: Kumamoto is a city in central Kyushu, Japan, and the capital of Kumamoto Prefecture. It grew around Kumamoto Castle, built by Katō Kiyomasa in the early 17th century and held by the Hosokawa from 1632 until the end of the Edo period.

kong-cote-divoire.s: Kong is a town in northern Côte d'Ivoire that grew from a Dyula trading town into the capital of the Kong Empire in the early 18th century. It was a centre of trade in gold, kola nuts and cloth and of Islamic learning, with mosques built in the Sudanese earthen style.

kaduna-river.s: The Kaduna River is a tributary of the Niger in central Nigeria. It rises on the Jos Plateau and flows west and south-west past the city of Kaduna, which takes its name from it, to join the Niger.

kotoko-people.s: The Kotoko are a people of the floodplains south of Lake Chad, along the Chari and Logone rivers in Cameroon, Chad and Nigeria. They are regarded as descendants of the Sao culture and organised themselves into small walled city-states such as Logone-Birni, Kousseri and Makari,…

krusevo.s: Kruševo is a mountain town in the south-west of North Macedonia, at about 1,350 metres one of the highest towns in the Balkans. A prosperous trading centre of Slav, Aromanian and Greek-oriented Orthodox families under Ottoman rule, it was seized by insurgents in the Ilinden…

krusevo-manifesto.s: The Kruševo Manifesto is a proclamation attributed to the insurgents who held Kruševo during the Ilinden Uprising of August 1903, addressed to the Muslim inhabitants of the surrounding villages. It called on them to join the struggle against Ottoman tyranny rather than treat…

krasnodar.s: Krasnodar is a city in southern Russia on the Kuban River and the capital of Krasnodar Krai. It was founded in 1793 by the Black Sea Cossacks as a fort named Yekaterinodar, after Catherine the Great, and became the capital of the Kuban Cossack Host.

kumamoto-prefecture.s: Kumamoto Prefecture is a prefecture in central Kyushu, Japan, with its capital at Kumamoto. It was formed in 1871 from the Kumamoto domain of the Hosokawa clan and covers the old province of Higo.

kato-tadahiro.s: Katō Tadahiro was the son and heir of Katō Kiyomasa, succeeding him as lord of Kumamoto in Higo in 1611 while still a boy. In 1632 the Tokugawa shogunate removed him from his domain and exiled him to Dewa province, where he died, and Higo was given to Hosokawa Tadatoshi.

kanishka.s: Kanishka was the most famous ruler of the Kushan Empire, reigning in the 2nd century CE, probably from about 127, over lands from Bactria to the Ganges plain, with capitals at Purushapura (Peshawar) and Mathura. The Rabatak inscription records his descent from Kujula Kadphises…

kant-kyrgyzstan.s: Kant is a town in the Chüy Valley of northern Kyrgyzstan, about 20 kilometres east of Bishkek, whose name means sugar in Kyrgyz, after the sugar refinery around which it grew. A former Soviet airfield there has been used as a Russian air base since 2003 under the Collective…

kumtor-gold-mine.s: The Kumtor Gold Mine is an open-pit gold mine high in the Tian Shan mountains of Kyrgyzstan, south of Lake Issyk-Kul, at about 4,000 metres. Developed with a Canadian company and producing from 1997, it became the country's largest industrial enterprise and a large share of…

kiso-river.s: The Kiso is a river of central Honshu, Japan, about 230 kilometres long, flowing from the mountains of Nagano Prefecture through Gifu and Aichi to Ise Bay. With the Nagara and Ibi it forms the Kiso Three Rivers, whose flood-prone delta was the scene of major Edo-period…

kuwana.s: Kuwana is a city in Mie Prefecture, Japan, at the mouth of the Kiso, Nagara and Ibi rivers on Ise Bay. In the Edo period it was a castle town, the seat of the Kuwana domain created for Honda Tadakatsu in 1601, and a post town on the Tokaido, where travellers took the ferry…

kurume.s: Kurume is a city in Fukuoka Prefecture, Japan, on the Chikugo river in northern Kyushu. From 1621 to 1871 it was the castle town of the Kurume domain, ruled by the Arima clan.

kausambi.s: Kaushambi was an ancient city on the Yamuna, about 50 kilometres south-west of Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh, India, and the capital of the Vatsa kingdom. One of the great cities of the Buddha's time, ruled by King Udayana, it lay on trade routes between the Ganges plain and the…

kwantung-government-general.s: The Kwantung Government-General was the Japanese administration of the Kwantung Leased Territory on the Liaodong peninsula, set up at Port Arthur in 1906 under General Ōshima Yoshimasa after Japan took over Russia's lease. Its governor-general, an army officer, also guarded…

kassel.s: Kassel is a city in northern Hesse, Germany, on the Fulda river. It was the residence of the landgraves of Hesse and from 1567 the capital of Hesse-Kassel, later the Electorate of Hesse, and from 1807 to 1813 the capital of Napoleon's Kingdom of Westphalia.

khorat-plateau.s: The Khorat Plateau is a broad, low plateau in north-eastern Thailand, bounded by the Mekong river to the north and east and by the Phetchabun and Dangrek ranges. It covers most of the Isan region, drained by the Mun and Chi rivers.

kudur-mabuk.s: Kudur-Mabuk was an Amorite chief of the Yamutbal tribe in the region east of the Tigris, whose name is Elamite. Around 1834 BCE he took control of Larsa and installed his son Warad-Sin as king, followed by another son, Rim-Sin I, while he himself kept the title of 'father of…

kirthar-mountains.s: The Kirthar Mountains are a range in south-western Pakistan, running about 300 kilometres north to south along the border between Sindh and Balochistan. They separate the lower Indus plain from the Balochistan uplands, and their southern part is protected as Kirthar National…

kayal.s: Kayal was a medieval port of the Pandya kingdom on the Gulf of Mannar coast of Tamil Nadu, India, near the mouth of the Tamraparni river and the modern town of Kayalpattinam. Marco Polo and the Persian historian Wassaf describe it as a busy harbour where Arab and Persian…

kalapi.s: Kalapi was the pen name of Sursinhji Takhtasinhji Gohil, ruler of the princely state of Lathi in Saurashtra, India, and a leading Gujarati poet. His romantic and melancholy poems, many in ghazal form and shaped by his unhappy personal life, were collected after his early death…

kalapino-kekarav.s: Kalapino Kekarav, 'the cry of Kalapi', is the collected poetry of the Gujarati poet Kalapi, ruler of Lathi, published after his death in 1900. Edited by his friend and fellow poet Kant, it contains some 250 poems on love, nature and grief, including well-known ghazals.

krka-river.s: The Krka is a river in Dalmatia, Croatia, about 73 km long, which flows past Knin to the Adriatic near Šibenik. Famous for its travertine waterfalls, now protected in the Krka National Park, it marked the southern limit of Liburnian territory in antiquity, with the town of…

karanga.s: The Karanga are a Shona-speaking people of southern Zimbabwe, the largest of the Shona subgroups. Their ancestors are associated with Great Zimbabwe and with the Mutapa and Rozvi states, and several South African ruling lines, including those of the Lobedu and the Venda, trace…

kharg-island.s: Kharg Island is a small island in the Persian Gulf off the coast of Iran, north-west of Bushehr. The Dutch East India Company built a fort and trading post there in the 1750s, which Mir Muhanna, lord of Bandar Rig, seized in the 1760s.

kumanovo.s: Kumanovo is a city in the north of North Macedonia, near the Serbian border. In the 14th century its district belonged to the Serbian magnate Dejan and his sons, the Dejanović lords, before Ottoman rule.

kerkennah-islands.s: The Kerkennah Islands are a low-lying group of islands in the Gulf of Gabès off the coast of Sfax in Tunisia. Inhabited since antiquity, they were known to the Romans as Cercina and have long lived from fishing.

kessinians.s: The Kessinians (Kessiner) were a West Slavic tribe of the Lutician federation on the lower Warnow river in modern Mecklenburg, Germany, around the later city of Rostock. In 1057 they and the Circipanians fought the Redarii and Tollensians for leadership of the federation.

kumara-kampana.s: Kumara Kampana was a prince and general of the Vijayanagara Empire, a son of Bukka Raya I. In the 1360s he conquered the Sambuvaraya kingdom around Kanchipuram, and around 1370–1378 he destroyed the Madurai Sultanate, bringing the Tamil country under Vijayanagara.

kharavela.s: Kharavela was a king of Kalinga, in modern Odisha, of the Mahameghavahana dynasty, who probably reigned in the 1st century BCE. He is known from the Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri, which records his public works, festivals and campaigns against the Satavahanas, Magadha…

kech-district.s: Kech is a district of Balochistan in south-western Pakistan, centred on the Kech valley and the town of Turbat. Its date-palm oases made it the heart of Makran, ruled in the 19th century by the Gichki family as vassals of the Khanate of Kalat.

kushinagar.s: Kushinagar, ancient Kusinara, is a town in eastern Uttar Pradesh, India, where according to Buddhist tradition the Buddha died and entered parinirvana. It was a centre of the Malla people, who cremated his body and shared out his relics.

kasur.s: Kasur is a city in the Punjab province of Pakistan, south-east of Lahore near the border with India. In the 18th century it was ruled by Pathan chiefs until Ranjit Singh annexed it around 1807.

khwarazmshah.s: Khwarazmshah ('Shah of Khwarazm') was the title of the rulers of Khwarazm, the oasis region on the lower Amu Darya south of the Aral Sea. It was borne by the Afrighid kings, then by the Ma'munids from 995, by Ghaznavid and Seljuq governors, and finally by the Anushtegin…

kathmandu.s: Kathmandu is the capital and largest city of Nepal, in the Kathmandu Valley in the Himalayan foothills. As Kantipur it was the seat of one of the three Malla kingdoms of the valley, whose rulers built much of its Durbar Square.

kyirong.s: Kyirong (Gyirong) is a county in Shigatse prefecture of Tibet, China, on the border with Nepal. Its valley, cut by a river flowing south through the Himalaya, has long been one of the easiest routes between Tibet and the Kathmandu Valley, carrying salt, grain and wool, and it…

klosterneuburg.s: Klosterneuburg is a town on the Danube just north of Vienna in Lower Austria. It was briefly a residence of the Babenberg margraves, and Leopold III founded its Augustinian abbey in 1114, which became the burial place of the saint and holds the enamelled Verdun Altar of…

karlsruhe.s: Karlsruhe is a city in Baden-Württemberg, Germany, founded in 1715 by Margrave Charles III William of Baden-Durlach as a new residence. It was planned in a fan shape, with streets radiating from the palace tower.

krosno-odrzanskie.s: Krosno Odrzańskie, in German Crossen an der Oder, is a town in western Poland at the confluence of the Bóbr and the Oder. A Silesian ducal town in the Middle Ages, it passed to Brandenburg in the late 15th century and later formed part of the lands of Margrave John of…

kostrzyn-nad-odra.s: Kostrzyn nad Odrą, in German Küstrin, is a town in western Poland where the Warta joins the Oder. Margrave John of Brandenburg-Küstrin made it his capital and a powerful fortress in the 16th century, and in 1730 the young Frederick the Great was imprisoned there.

kralice-bible.s: The Kralice Bible is the first complete Czech translation of the Bible from the original Hebrew and Greek, made by scholars of the Unity of the Brethren and printed at Kralice nad Oslavou in Moravia in six volumes between 1579 and 1593. Its language became the model for…

kamenz.s: Kamenz is a town in Upper Lusatia in Saxony, Germany, near the Sorbian-speaking area. In 1346 it was one of the founding members of the Six Towns League of Upper Lusatia, formed to protect trade.

kotagede.s: Kotagede is a historic district of the city of Yogyakarta in central Java, Indonesia. It was the first capital of the Mataram Sultanate, built up in the late sixteenth century by Ki Ageng Pemanahan and his son Panembahan Senapati, whose graves lie beside its old royal mosque.

kuru-kingdom.s: The Kuru kingdom was a Vedic Indo-Aryan realm of northern India, centred on the upper Ganges–Yamuna region around present-day Haryana and Delhi, in roughly 1200–500 BCE. It played a major part in shaping Vedic ritual and the collection of the Vedic texts.

kedu-plain.s: The Kedu Plain is a fertile volcanic basin in Central Java, Indonesia, ringed by the volcanoes Merapi, Merbabu, Sumbing and Sindoro. Its rice fields supported the Medang kingdom and the Sailendra dynasty in the eighth and ninth centuries, and it holds major monuments of that…

kewu-plain.s: The Kewu Plain, also called the Prambanan Plain, is a fertile area in Central Java, Indonesia, on the southern slopes of Mount Merapi near Yogyakarta. In the eighth and ninth centuries it was a heartland of the Medang kingdom and the Sailendra dynasty, and it holds a dense…

karang-brahi-inscription.s: The Karang Brahi inscription is a Srivijayan stone inscription in Old Malay, found in 1904 on the upper Merangin river in Jambi, Sumatra. Undated, it is usually placed close to the Kota Kapur inscription of 686 because its curse formula is almost the same.

kota-kapur-inscription.s: The Kota Kapur inscription is a stone inscription in Old Malay, found in 1892 on the island of Bangka off south-eastern Sumatra and dated 686 CE. Issued by Srivijaya, it lays down curses on those who rebel against the ruler and mentions an expedition against Java.

karabakh.s: Karabakh is a region of the South Caucasus, between the Lesser Caucasus mountains and the Kura and Aras rivers, today in Azerbaijan. Its highlands, long home to Armenian princes and meliks, and its lowland pastures were ruled in turn by Persian, Turkic and local dynasties,…

klima-milos.s: Klima is a fishing village on the island of Milos (Melos) in the Cyclades, Greece, on the north side of the island's large natural harbour. Above it lie the remains of the ancient city of Melos, with its walls, theatre and early Christian catacombs, and the Venus de Milo was…

kayqubad-i.s: Kayqubad I was sultan of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum in Anatolia from 1220 to 1237, the period of its greatest power. He took Alanya, which he rebuilt as a winter capital, extended Seljuk rule in eastern Anatolia, absorbing the Mengujekid lands of Erzincan, and built…

kemah.s: Kemah is a small town on the upper Euphrates in Erzincan province, eastern Turkey, below a strong fortress on a rock above the river gorge. Known in Byzantine times as Kamacha, it was one of the seats of the Mengujekid emirs from the late eleventh century, and later passed to…

kazybek-bi.s: Kazybek Bi was a Kazakh judge, orator and diplomat of the Middle Juz, one of the three great biys traditionally linked with Tauke Khan's law code, the Zhety Zhargy or 'Seven Charters', together with Tole Bi and Aiteke Bi. Famed for his eloquence and called 'the goose-voiced',…

karabel-relief.s: The Karabel relief is a Late Bronze Age rock carving at the Karabel pass near Izmir in western Turkey, showing a warrior with bow and spear accompanied by a Luwian hieroglyphic inscription. Herodotus took it for an image of the Egyptian king Sesostris.

kirana-gharana.s: The Kirana gharana is one of the main stylistic schools of Hindustani classical singing, named after the town of Kirana in Uttar Pradesh. It was shaped in the late 19th and early 20th centuries by Abdul Karim Khan, who settled at Miraj, and Abdul Wahid Khan, and is known for…

kru-people.s: The Kru are a West African people of the coast of south-eastern Liberia and south-western Côte d'Ivoire, speaking Kru languages. From the 18th century they became renowned as sailors and dock workers, serving on European ships along the West African coast and settling in ports…

kinai.s: The Kinai, 'the home provinces', was the region around the old Japanese capitals of Nara and Kyoto, made up of the five provinces of Yamashiro, Yamato, Kawachi, Izumi and Settsu. As the land of the imperial court and later of the Ashikaga shoguns, it was the political and…

kachin-people.s: The Kachin are a group of related peoples of the hills of northern Myanmar and neighbouring parts of China and India, the largest of them the Jingpo. Traditionally living by swidden farming under hereditary chiefs, they long interacted with the Shan princes of the valleys.

kachin-state.s: Kachin State is the northernmost state of Myanmar, bordering China and India, with its capital at Myitkyina. Its mountains and the upper Irrawaddy valley are home to the Kachin peoples and to Shan and Burman communities, and it includes the jade mines of Hpakant.

kahnawake.s: Kahnawake is a Mohawk community on the south shore of the St Lawrence opposite Montreal, in Quebec. It grew from a Jesuit mission founded in 1667 that drew Catholic Mohawks and other Iroquois from New York, among them Kateri Tekakwitha.

kanesatake.s: Kanesatake is a Mohawk community on the Ottawa river west of Montreal, in Quebec, next to the town of Oka. It originated in a Sulpician mission founded in the early 18th century, and its people's long dispute over land with the Sulpicians and the town led in 1990 to the Oka…

kateri-tekakwitha.s: Kateri Tekakwitha was a Mohawk-Algonquin woman born in the Mohawk valley of New York who converted to Catholicism and moved to the Jesuit mission of Kahnawake near Montreal. Known for her strict piety and penances, she died at the age of 24.

karyes.s: Karyes is the administrative centre of the monastic state of Mount Athos in northern Greece. It is the seat of the Holy Community, the council of representatives of the twenty ruling monasteries, and of its executive, as well as of a civil governor appointed by the Greek state.

krusevac.s: Kruševac is a city in central Serbia on the West Morava river. In the 1370s Prince Lazar made it the capital of his state, building a fortress and the court church of Lazarica, and from there he led his army to the Battle of Kosovo in 1389.

kikkawa-clan.s: The Kikkawa were a Japanese warrior clan of Aki province, in western Honshu. In the 16th century Mōri Motonari placed his son Motoharu at its head, and with the Kobayakawa it became one of the 'two rivers' supporting the Mōri.

kobayakawa-clan.s: The Kobayakawa were a Japanese warrior clan of Aki province in western Honshu. In the 16th century Mōri Motonari placed his son Takakage at its head, and with the Kikkawa it became one of the 'two rivers' supporting the Mōri.

kiram-bates-treaty.s: The Kiram-Bates Treaty was an agreement signed in August 1899 between the United States, represented by General John C. Bates, and Sultan Jamalul Kiram II of Sulu.

khazen-family.s: The Khazen family is a Maronite noble family of Mount Lebanon, whose sheikhs held the Keserwan district as tax-farming lords from the 17th century under the Ma'n and Shihab emirs. They were patrons of the Maronite Church and gained French consular posts.

keserwan.s: Keserwan is a mountainous district of Mount Lebanon, north of Beirut, inhabited mainly by Maronite Christians. From the 17th century it was dominated by the Khazen sheikhs under the emirs of Mount Lebanon.

koe-thaung-temple.s: The Koe-thaung Temple is a large Buddhist temple at Mrauk U in Rakhine State, Myanmar, built by King Min Dikkha in the mid-16th century. Its name means 'shrine of the 90,000 images', after the many carved Buddha images lining its galleries.

kitab-al-itibar.s: The Kitab al-I'tibar, or Book of Contemplation, is the memoir of the Syrian Arab nobleman Usama ibn Munqidh, written in his old age around 1183. Its anecdotes of hunting, warfare, medicine and daily life, including vivid descriptions of the customs of the Frankish crusaders,…

kitob.s: Kitob is a town in the Qashqadaryo region of southern Uzbekistan, close to Shahrisabz. Under the emirate of Bukhara it formed with Shahrisabz an oasis of semi-independent Uzbek beks, who repeatedly resisted Bukharan rule until the Russians handed the area to Bukhara in 1870.

kyawswa-of-pagan.s: Kyawswa was king of Pagan in Burma from 1289 to 1297. He inherited a kingdom broken by the Mongol invasions and controlled little more than the capital, while three brothers held the Kyaukse district.

krishna-raja-sagara.s: Krishna Raja Sagara is a dam and reservoir on the Kaveri River near Mysore in Karnataka, India, named after Maharaja Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV. Built between 1911 and 1931 under the direction of the engineer M.

krishnaraja-wodeyar-iv.s: Krishnaraja Wodeyar IV was Maharaja of Mysore from 1894 to 1940, ruling with full powers from 1902. With diwans such as M.

kobayashi-torasaburo.s: Kobayashi Torasaburo was a senior retainer of the Nagaoka domain in Japan. After the domain's defeat in the Boshin War, it received a hundred sacks of rice as relief in 1870, and he used them to fund a school rather than distribute them to its hungry samurai.

kuberanaga.s: Kuberanaga was a princess of the Naga dynasty who married the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II in the late 4th century. Her daughter Prabhavatigupta married the Vakataka king Rudrasena II and later ruled the Vakataka kingdom as regent, linking the Gupta, Naga and Vakataka houses.

kangarlu.s: The Kangarlu were a Turkic tribe of the Nakhchivan region in the South Caucasus. Under Safavid and Afsharid rule they supplied local governors, and after Nader Shah's death in 1747 their chief Haydar Quli Khan founded the Nakhichevan Khanate, which his family ruled until the…

kuomintang.s: The Kuomintang, or Chinese Nationalist Party, is a political party founded by Sun Yat-sen and his allies in 1912, growing out of the revolutionary Tongmenghui. Under Chiang Kai-shek it reunited much of China through the Northern Expedition and ruled the Republic of China from…

kit-carson.s: Kit Carson was an American frontiersman, trapper and guide who became famous through John C. Frémont's western expeditions of the 1840s.

kelmis.s: Kelmis, in French La Calamine, is a municipality in the German-speaking Community of Belgium near Aachen. Its zinc mine, the Vieille Montagne, was so valuable that the Netherlands and Prussia left it in the neutral condominium of Neutral Moresnet from 1816 until the territory…

kanak-people.s: The Kanak are the indigenous Melanesian people of New Caledonia, making up about 40 per cent of its population. French colonisation from 1853 confined them to reserves and provoked major revolts in 1878 and 1917.

kalmar-nyckel.s: The Kalmar Nyckel was a Dutch-built armed merchant ship that carried the first Swedish colonists to North America. Sailing with the smaller Fogel Grip under Peter Minuit, it reached the Delaware River in March 1638, where the settlers founded Fort Christina, the beginning of…

kapisa.s: Kapisa was an ancient city and region north of Kabul, at modern Begram near Bagram in Afghanistan. It was a summer capital of the Kushan Empire, and a hoard of Indian ivories, Roman glass and Chinese lacquer found there shows its place in long-distance trade.

kshatriya.s: Kshatriya is the second of the four varnas of the traditional Hindu social order, the class of rulers and warriors, ranked after the Brahmins. Vedic and later texts assign to Kshatriyas the duties of protecting the people, governing and waging war.

karonga.s: Karonga is a town on the north-western shore of Lake Malawi, in the Northern Region of Malawi. Its plain was the heart of the Ngonde kingdom of the Kyungu rulers.

khartoum.s: Khartoum is the capital of Sudan, at the meeting of the Blue and White Niles. It was founded as an Egyptian army camp in the 1820s and became the seat of the Turco-Egyptian administration of the Sudan.

kadazan-dusun.s: The Kadazan-Dusun are the largest Indigenous group of Sabah, the Malaysian state in northern Borneo, a collective name for the closely related Kadazan and Dusun peoples who speak Dusunic languages. Traditionally rice farmers of the west coast and the interior, many became…

kafue-river.s: The Kafue is a river of Zambia, about 960 km long and the largest tributary of the Zambezi lying wholly within the country. It rises near the Congo border, flows past the Copperbelt, crosses the wide Kafue Flats and joins the Zambezi downstream of Kariba.

kanno-disturbance.s: The Kannō disturbance was a conflict of 1350 to 1352 within the Ashikaga shogunate of Japan, between the shogun Ashikaga Takauji and his brother Tadayoshi, who for a time allied with the Southern Court. Southern forces exploited the split to seize Kyoto in 1352 and carry off…

konjikido.s: The Konjikidō, or Golden Hall, is a small Buddhist hall at Chūson-ji in Hiraizumi, northern Japan, completed in 1124 under Fujiwara no Kiyohira. Its interior and exterior are covered with gold leaf and black lacquer inlaid with mother-of-pearl, and it houses an Amida Buddha…

kiyohara-clan.s: The Kiyohara were a warrior family of Dewa province in northern Japan. They helped the Minamoto defeat the Abe clan in the Former Nine Years' War of 1051 to 1062 and took over the Abe lands in Mutsu.

kenneth-kaunda.s: Kenneth Kaunda was the first president of Zambia, from independence in 1964 until 1991. Born at Lubwa mission in northern Zambia, he led the United National Independence Party in the campaign against the Central African Federation.

kalomo.s: Kalomo is a town in Southern Province, Zambia, on the railway between Livingstone and Lusaka. It was the first administrative capital of North-Western Rhodesia under the British South Africa Company, from about 1899 until the seat moved to Livingstone in 1907.

kaunas.s: Kaunas, historically Kovno, is the second-largest city of Lithuania, at the confluence of the Neris and Nemunas rivers. Grown around a 14th-century castle, it was the seat of the German Ober Ost military administration during the First World War and served as Lithuania's…

kanagawa-prefecture.s: Kanagawa Prefecture is a prefecture of Japan on the south-west side of Tokyo Bay, with its capital at Yokohama. It covers the former province of Sagami and part of Musashi, including the old castle town of Odawara, and was formed after the abolition of the domains in 1871.

kazanlak.s: Kazanlak is a town in central Bulgaria, in the Valley of Roses south of the Balkan Mountains. Nearby lie the remains of the Odrysian royal city of Seuthopolis and the Kazanlak Tomb, a Thracian tomb with wall paintings of about 300 BCE that is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

koraku-en.s: Kōraku-en is a landscape garden in Okayama, Japan, built for the daimyo Ikeda Tsunamasa of the Okayama Domain and completed in 1700. A stroll garden of lawns, ponds, tea houses and borrowed views of Okayama Castle, it was opened to the public in 1884.

kumazawa-banzan.s: Kumazawa Banzan was a Japanese Confucian scholar of the Wang Yangming school and a pupil of Nakae Tōju. In the service of Ikeda Mitsumasa of the Okayama Domain he advised on government, flood control and famine relief, and helped shape the domain's reforms.

kotrag.s: Kotrag was a Bulgar leader of the 7th century, by tradition a son of Kubrat of Old Great Bulgaria. When Khazar pressure broke up his father's realm after Kubrat's death, he led his followers north to the middle Volga, where their settlement became the basis of Volga Bulgaria.

khafre.s: Khafre was a king of Egypt's Fourth Dynasty in the 26th century BCE and a son of Khufu. He built the second pyramid at Giza, and the Great Sphinx is generally attributed to his reign.

khufu.s: Khufu was a king of Egypt's Fourth Dynasty in the 26th century BCE and the son of Sneferu. He built the Great Pyramid at Giza, the largest of the Egyptian pyramids and one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World.

kiyosu.s: Kiyosu is a city in Aichi Prefecture, Japan, north-west of Nagoya. Its castle was the base of Oda Nobunaga during his rise to power and the scene of the Kiyosu Conference of 1582 that followed his death.

korps-marechaussee-te-voet.s: The Korps Marechaussee te voet was a Dutch colonial counter-insurgency force formed in Aceh in 1890. Its small, mobile brigades of Indonesian soldiers under Dutch officers, armed with carbines and the klewang sword, pursued guerrillas through jungle and hills.

keryneia.s: Keryneia, or Ceryneia, was an ancient town of Achaea in the northern Peloponnese, in the hills south of Helike. Pausanias records that refugees from Mycenae settled there after Argos destroyed their city in the 5th century BCE.

kamrup.s: Kamrup is the historical region of western Assam around Guwahati, in the lower Brahmaputra valley of north-east India. It takes its name from the ancient kingdom of Kamarupa and in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries was contested between the Koch kingdoms, the Mughal…

kelafo.s: Kelafo, also spelled Qalaafo, is a town on the Shebelle river in the Somali Region of Ethiopia. Somali tradition places one of the centres of the Ajuran Sultanate there, controlling the water and farmland of the upper Shebelle valley.

kaiseraugst.s: Kaiseraugst is a village in the canton of Aargau, Switzerland, on the Rhine east of Basel. It grew from the late Roman fortress of Castrum Rauracense, built around 300 beside the colony of Augusta Raurica to guard the Rhine crossing against the Alemanni.

kitab-i-diyarbakriyya.s: The Kitab-i Diyarbakriyya is a Persian chronicle of the Aq Qoyunlu dynasty written by Abu Bakr Tihrani for Uzun Hasan in the later fifteenth century. It recounts the rise of the Bayandur Turkmen princes from their base around Diyarbakır and supports their legitimacy with a…

kashtiliash-iv.s: Kashtiliash IV was a Kassite king of Babylon in the thirteenth century BCE. Around 1225 BCE he was defeated and captured by the Assyrian king Tukulti-Ninurta I, who carried him in chains to Assur and took control of Babylon, a victory celebrated in the Assyrian poem known as…

kerameikos.s: The Kerameikos was the potters' quarter of ancient Athens, lying on both sides of the city wall north-west of the Acropolis, and the site of the city's main cemetery. Its graves, excavated since the nineteenth century, provide a continuous record from the Bronze Age onwards,…

karl-philipp-prince-of-schwarzenberg.s: Karl Philipp, Prince of Schwarzenberg, was an Austrian field marshal and diplomat who commanded the Austrian auxiliary corps in Napoleon's invasion of Russia in 1812. After Austria joined the Sixth Coalition in 1813 he became commander-in-chief of the allied armies, which…

kromeriz.s: Kroměříž, in German Kremsier, is a town in Moravia in the Czech Republic, long the summer seat of the bishops and archbishops of Olomouc, whose palace and gardens are a UNESCO World Heritage Site. From November 1848 to March 1849 the Austrian Reichstag sat there and drafted a…

kalahom.s: The Kalahom was one of the two great ministries of the Siamese state from the Ayutthaya period, headed by the Samuha Kalahom and responsible originally for military affairs and later for the administration of the southern provinces. Traditionally attributed to the reforms of…

kosa-pan.s: Kosa Pan was a Siamese diplomat who led King Narai's embassy to France, received by Louis XIV at Versailles in 1686. The great curiosity aroused by the Siamese envoys made the embassy famous in France.

kalimullah-shah.s: Kalimullah Shah was the last sultan of the Bahmani Sultanate, a puppet of the Barid family at Bidar. Around 1527 he fled the city and appealed for help to Babur, the new Mughal ruler of Delhi, and then to the sultans of Bijapur and Ahmadnagar, but found no effective support…

krishnadevaraya.s: Krishnadevaraya was emperor of Vijayanagara from 1509 to 1529, of the Tuluva dynasty, and the most celebrated ruler of the empire. He defeated the Deccan sultanates, took the Raichur Doab from Bijapur in 1520 and conquered coastal Andhra from the Gajapatis of Odisha.

kwando-river.s: The Kwando is a river of southern Africa that rises in the highlands of Angola and flows south-east along the Angola–Zambia border before crossing the Caprivi Strip of Namibia, where it is known lower down as the Linyanti and the Chobe. It formed the western limit of the lands…

karrani-dynasty.s: The Karrani dynasty was an Afghan dynasty that ruled Bengal from 1564 to 1576, the last independent sultans of Bengal. Taj Khan Karrani took Gaur in 1564, and his brother Sulaiman Khan Karrani moved the capital to Tanda, conquered Orissa in 1568 and outwardly acknowledged Akbar.
