kasimov.s: Kasimov is a town on the Oka river in Ryazan Oblast, Russia. Originally called Gorodets Meshchersky, it was granted in 1452 by Grand Prince Vasily II of Moscow to the Tatar prince Qasim, son of Ulugh Muhammad, and became the seat of the Qasim Khanate, a Muscovite vassal ruled…

karatepe.s: Karatepe is a Neo-Hittite fortress in the Taurus foothills of Osmaniye province, southern Turkey, built in the late 8th or early 7th century BCE by Azatiwada, a vassal of the kings of Que. Excavated from 1947 by Helmuth Bossert and Halet Çambel, its gate reliefs carry long…

kousseri.s: Kousseri is a town in the Far North Region of Cameroon, on the Logone river opposite N'Djamena, capital of Chad. Once one of the walled Kotoko city-states, it gave its name to the Battle of Kousseri of 22 April 1900, in which French columns destroyed the army of Rabih…

kuching.s: Kuching is the capital of Sarawak, Malaysia, on the Sarawak River in north-western Borneo. A small Malay trading settlement under Brunei, it became the capital of James Brooke's Raj of Sarawak in 1841 and grew under the Brooke rajahs, whose Astana palace and Fort Margherita…

kalb-ali-khan.s: Kalb Ali Khan was Nawab of Rampur in northern India from 1865 to 1887. A poet and scholar of Arabic and Persian, he enlarged the state library that became the Raza Library and made his court a refuge for poets and musicians from Delhi and Lucknow, among them the Urdu poet Dagh…

kailasa-temple-ellora.s: The Kailasa temple at Ellora in Maharashtra, India, is a Hindu temple to Shiva carved downward from a single mass of basalt rock. Commissioned by the Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century, it reproduces a free-standing temple complex with shrine, halls, gateway and…

kavirajamarga.s: The Kavirajamarga ('Royal Road of Poets') is the earliest surviving literary work in Kannada, a treatise on poetics written in the 9th century at the court of the Rashtrakuta emperor Amoghavarsha I. Attributed to the king himself or to his court poet Srivijaya, it adapts…

krishna-iii.s: Krishna III was the last great emperor of the Rashtrakuta dynasty, ruling the Deccan from 939 to 967. In 949 he defeated the Chola army at Takkolam, where the Chola crown prince Rajaditya was killed, and occupied the northern Chola lands for some years.

kondapalli.s: Kondapalli is a town near Vijayawada in Andhra Pradesh, India, known for its hill fort and its brightly painted wooden toys. The fort was a stronghold of the Reddi kings in the 14th and 15th centuries and later passed through several dynasties before coming under the British.

kondavidu.s: Kondavidu is a hill fort in Guntur district, Andhra Pradesh, India. In the 14th century it became the capital of the Reddi Kingdom, whose kings ruled coastal Andhra from it until Vijayanagara forces took it around 1424.

kinmen.s: Kinmen, also called Quemoy, is a group of islands governed by the Republic of China (Taiwan) lying only a few kilometres off the city of Xiamen in mainland China. Nationalist forces repelled a Communist landing at the Battle of Guningtou in 1949, and the islands were heavily…

kaiyo-maru.s: The Kaiyō Maru was a steam frigate built in the Netherlands for the Tokugawa shogunate and delivered in 1867, then the most powerful warship in Japan. Enomoto Takeaki took it north to Hokkaido in 1868, but it ran aground and sank in a storm off Esashi late that year.

k-j-stahlberg.s: Kaarlo Juho Ståhlberg was a Finnish lawyer and the first president of the Republic of Finland, serving from 1919 to 1925. As the main author of the republican constitution of 1919, he worked to heal the divisions of the civil war, pardoning many imprisoned Reds.

keflavik.s: Keflavík is a town on the Reykjanes peninsula in south-western Iceland, now part of the municipality of Reykjanesbær. Its airport, Iceland's main international gateway, began as a US military airfield in the Second World War.

kallergis-family.s: The Kallergis were a powerful Greek noble family of Crete under Venetian rule, claiming descent from Byzantine aristocracy. Alexios Kallergis led a long revolt against Venice from 1282 that ended in 1299 with a treaty granting the family privileges and Venetian noble status.

kawit.s: Kawit is a town in Cavite province on Manila Bay in the Philippines and the birthplace of Emilio Aguinaldo. On 12 June 1898 Aguinaldo proclaimed Philippine independence from Spain from his house there, a date now celebrated as Independence Day.

keiskamma-river.s: The Keiskamma River flows south-east through the Eastern Cape province of South Africa into the Indian Ocean. In the frontier wars of the 19th century it marked one of the successive boundaries between the Cape Colony and the Xhosa, and the land between the Keiskamma and the…

karmapa.s: The Karmapa is the head of the Karma Kagyu school of Tibetan Buddhism and the oldest line of reincarnated lamas in Tibet, beginning with Düsum Khyenpa in the 12th century. The Karmapas were patrons and allies of the Rinpungpa and Tsangpa rulers of Tsang in the 15th to 17th…

kojiki.s: The Kojiki ('Record of Ancient Matters') is the oldest surviving Japanese chronicle, compiled by Ō no Yasumaro and presented to the court in 712. It recounts the myths of the creation of Japan and the descent of the imperial line from the sun goddess Amaterasu, followed by…

kintyre.s: Kintyre is a long peninsula in the south-west of Argyll, Scotland, whose southern tip, the Mull of Kintyre, lies about 20 kilometres from Ireland. It was the heartland of the Cenél nGabráin, one of the ruling kindreds of Dál Riata, and later part of the Kingdom of the Isles…

karmoy.s: Karmøy is an island in Rogaland on the west coast of Norway, separated from the mainland by the Karmsund strait. It holds the royal site of Avaldsnes and many Iron Age and Viking-age monuments.

karmsund.s: Karmsund (Karmsundet) is a narrow strait on the west coast of Norway between the island of Karmøy and the mainland near Haugesund. As a sheltered part of the coastal sea route, the 'North Way' that gave Norway its name, it was controlled by the kings who sat at Avaldsnes.

katehr.s: Katehr was the medieval name of the region east of the Ganges in today's Uttar Pradesh, India, later known as Rohilkhand. Its Rajput chiefs resisted the Delhi Sultanate and the Mughals, and from the late 17th century Afghan settlers, the Rohillas, made it the base of their own…

kodiak-island.s: Kodiak Island is a large island off the south coast of Alaska, home of the Alutiiq people. In 1784 Grigory Shelikhov founded the first permanent Russian settlement in America at Three Saints Bay there, and the town of Kodiak was the capital of Russian America until 1808, when…

kigali.s: Kigali is the capital and largest city of Rwanda, in the hills at the centre of the country. It began as a German residency founded in 1907 and grew rapidly after it became the capital at independence in 1962.

kutahya.s: Kütahya is a city in western Anatolia, Turkey, the ancient Cotyaeum. From the late 13th century it was the capital of the Germiyanid beylik, which passed to the Ottomans in 1429.

kobe.s: Kobe is a port city in western Japan on Osaka Bay, capital of Hyogo Prefecture. Its old harbour of Hyogo, known in the 12th century as Owada no Tomari, was developed by Taira no Kiyomori and was a chief port for trade with China until the Onin War.

kilamuwa.s: Kilamuwa was a king of Sam'al, a kingdom in south-eastern Anatolia, in the later 9th century BCE. His inscription, carved in Phoenician on a stone slab found at Zincirli in 1902, boasts that he hired the king of Assyria against his enemies and improved the lot of his poorest…

kuttamuwa-stele.s: The Kuttamuwa stele is a basalt funerary monument found in 2008 at Zincirli in south-eastern Turkey, ancient Sam'al. Set up around 735 BCE by Kuttamuwa, an official of King Panamuwa II, it shows him at a funerary feast, and its inscription asks that offerings be made for his…

khunzakh.s: Khunzakh is a village in the mountains of central Dagestan, Russia, on a plateau above the Avar Koysu river. It was the centre of the early medieval kingdom of Sarir and later the seat of the Avar khans, who ruled much of mountainous Dagestan until the Russian conquest.

kagoshima-prefecture.s: Kagoshima Prefecture is a prefecture of Japan at the southern tip of Kyushu, including the Satsuma and Osumi peninsulas and a chain of islands reaching towards Okinawa. It was created in 1871 from the lands of the Satsuma Domain, whose Shimazu lords had ruled the region for…

kosrae.s: Kosrae is a volcanic island in the eastern Caroline Islands of the western Pacific, and one of the four states of the Federated States of Micronesia. Between about 1250 and 1400 its chiefdoms were united under a paramount ruler, the Tokosra, who governed from the stone city of…

kaliningrad-oblast.s: Kaliningrad Oblast is a Russian exclave on the Baltic Sea between Poland and Lithuania, centred on the city of Kaliningrad, formerly Königsberg. It occupies the northern part of the former German province of East Prussia, home in the Middle Ages to Old Prussian peoples such as…

kashshu-nadin-ahi.s: Kashshu-nadin-ahi was the last king of the Second Sealand Dynasty, ruling Babylon for about three years around 1007 to 1005 BCE. A later text records that during his reign shortages and famine caused the regular offerings at the temple of Shamash in Sippar to cease.

kyrgyz-people.s: The Kyrgyz are a Turkic people of Central Asia who form the majority of the population of Kyrgyzstan and also live in China, Tajikistan and Afghanistan. Traditionally mountain pastoralists of the Tian Shan, they were subject in turn to Moghulistan, the Dzungars and the Khanate…

klang-war.s: The Klang War was a civil war in Selangor fought from 1867 to 1874 between rival Malay chiefs over control of the rich tin-mining districts and their river tolls. Chinese mining factions and secret societies joined opposing sides, and Yap Ah Loy's backing helped the Sultan's…

kuala-selangor.s: Kuala Selangor is a town at the mouth of the Selangor River on the west coast of Peninsular Malaysia. In the 18th century it was the seat of the first Sultans of Selangor, defended by a fort on Bukit Melawati overlooking the estuary.

kerbogha.s: Kerbogha was a Turkish commander who served the Seljuks as atabeg of Mosul. In 1098 he led a large Muslim army to relieve Antioch from the First Crusade, but the crusaders, who had just taken the city, defeated him outside its walls in June 1098.

kulinism.s: Kulinism was a system of ranking among Bengali Brahmins and Kayasthas that placed certain families, the Kulins, at the top of the social order. Tradition credits its creation to the Sena king Ballal Sena in the 12th century.

kinzua-dam.s: The Kinzua Dam is a flood-control dam on the Allegheny River in Pennsylvania, completed in 1965. Its reservoir flooded about 10,000 acres of the Seneca Nation's Allegany land and the Cornplanter Grant, forcing some 600 Seneca to leave their homes.

kufra.s: Kufra is a group of oases in the Libyan Desert of south-eastern Libya. In 1895 the Senussi order moved its headquarters there, making it a hub of the caravan trade between Cyrenaica and Wadai.

kamose.s: Kamose was the last king of the Seventeenth Dynasty of Egypt, ruling from Thebes. He campaigned north against the Hyksos and reached the walls of their capital Avaris, as recorded on his stelae at Karnak.

korti.s: Korti is a town on the Nile in northern Sudan, near the fourth cataract, in the land of the Shaigiya. In 1820 the Egyptian army of Ismail Pasha defeated the Shaigiya cavalry there with firearms during the conquest of Sudan.

kongoda.s: Kongoda was a historical region on the coast of southern Odisha, India, around modern Ganjam and the Chilika lake. From the 6th century it was ruled by the Shailodbhava dynasty, often as vassals of larger powers.

kapilavastu.s: Kapilavastu was the ancient city of the Shakya clan, in whose territory the Buddha grew up in the 5th or 6th century BCE. Its exact site is disputed between Tilaurakot in Nepal and Piprahwa in India, both with remains of the period.

kimweri-ye-nyumbai.s: Kimweri ye Nyumbai was king of the Shambaa in the Usambara Mountains of north-eastern Tanzania during the first half of the 19th century. Under him the Kilindi kingdom reached its greatest extent, ruling the mountains through sons placed as chiefs and receiving tribute from…

khazal-ibn-jabir.s: Khaz'al ibn Jabir was the Arab sheikh of Mohammerah, modern Khorramshahr, who from 1897 ruled much of Khuzestan as a semi-independent prince under nominal Qajar sovereignty. A close ally of Britain, he leased the land at Abadan on which the Anglo-Persian Oil Company built its…

khalid-bin-mohammed-al-qasimi.s: Khalid bin Mohammed Al Qasimi was ruler of Sharjah from 1965, when Britain deposed his cousin Saqr bin Sultan, until 1972. He accepted a memorandum of understanding with Iran over Abu Musa in November 1971 and took Sharjah into the United Arab Emirates at its founding that…

kagoshima.s: Kagoshima is a city on Kagoshima Bay in southern Kyushu, Japan, facing the active volcano Sakurajima. It was the castle town of the Shimazu lords of Satsuma, where Francis Xavier landed in 1549, and a British squadron bombarded it in 1863.

khalilullah-i.s: Khalilullah I was Shirvanshah from 1417 to 1465, son of Ibrahim I of the Derbendi line. His reign of almost half a century gave Shirvan its longest period of peace and prosperity, based on silk, oil and Caspian trade.

kale-akte.s: Kale Akte, Latin Calacte, was an ancient town on the north coast of Sicily, at modern Caronia. It was founded around 446 BCE by the Sicel leader Ducetius after his return from exile in Corinth.

karad.s: Karad is a town in Satara district, Maharashtra, India, at the confluence of the Krishna and Koyna rivers. An ancient settlement with early Buddhist rock-cut caves nearby, it lay in the heartland of the Silahara dynasty of Kolhapur, who arose in the region in the 10th century.

kopeshvara-temple.s: The Kopeshvara Temple is a Hindu temple to Shiva at Khidrapur on the Krishna river in Kolhapur district, Maharashtra, India. Begun under the Silahara dynasty of Kolhapur in the 12th century and completed under the Yadavas in the early 13th century, it is famed for its richly…

kharkiv.s: Kharkiv is the second-largest city of Ukraine, in the north-east of the country near the Russian border. Founded around 1654 as a fortress of Sloboda Ukraine, it grew into a centre of learning, with a university from 1805, and of heavy industry.

kharkiv-collegium.s: The Kharkiv Collegium was an Orthodox school in Kharkiv, founded in 1726 when Bishop Epifaniy Tikhorsky moved the Belgorod seminary there. Modelled on the Kyiv-Mohyla Academy, it taught Latin, rhetoric, philosophy and theology and was the leading school of Sloboda Ukraine in…

kitabatake-chikafusa.s: Kitabatake Chikafusa (1293–1354) was a Japanese courtier, general and writer, a leading supporter of Emperor Go-Daigo and the Southern Court. He fought the Ashikaga in eastern Japan, held out in Hitachi province for several years, and in 1339 wrote the Jinnō Shōtōki to defend…

koror.s: Koror is the largest town of Palau in the western Pacific and was its capital until 2006, when the seat of government moved to Ngerulmud. Under Japanese rule it was the headquarters of the South Seas Government from 1922 and grew into a sizeable town with a large Japanese…

keelung.s: Keelung is a port city on the northern tip of Taiwan. The Spanish occupied its harbour in 1626, building Fort San Salvador on Heping Island, until the Dutch took it in 1642.

king-ling-of-chu.s: King Ling of Chu (died 529 BCE) was a ruler of the State of Chu who seized the throne in 541 BCE by murdering his nephew, the reigning king. Ambitious and extravagant, he built the lavish Zhanghua Terrace, held a great interstate assembly and annexed the states of Chen and Cai.

king-hui-of-chu.s: King Hui of Chu (reigned 488–432 BCE) was a ruler of the State of Chu who restored its power after the Wu invasion of 506 BCE. He survived a revolt by his kinsman Bai Gong Sheng in 479 BCE and in the same year annexed the State of Chen, later also absorbing Cai.

king-zhuang-of-chu.s: King Zhuang of Chu (reigned 613–591 BCE) was a ruler of the State of Chu, counted among the Five Hegemons of the Spring and Autumn period. He crushed the powerful Ruo'ao lineage in 605 BCE, is said to have asked a Zhou envoy about the weight of the royal cauldrons, a sign of…

king-mu-of-chu.s: King Mu of Chu (reigned 625–614 BCE) was a ruler of the State of Chu who came to power in 626 BCE by forcing his father, King Cheng, to commit suicide. He continued Chu's expansion into the Huai River valley, destroying the State of Jiang in 623 BCE and other small states…

king-kaolie-of-chu.s: King Kaolie of Chu (reigned 262–238 BCE) was a ruler of the State of Chu in the late Warring States period. Guided by his chancellor Lord Chunshen, he annexed the State of Lu, led an alliance against Qin and moved the capital to Shouchun in 241 BCE.

king-xiao-of-zhou.s: King Xiao of Zhou was a king of the Western Zhou dynasty in the early 9th century BCE, conventionally dated c. 891–886 BCE.

king-li-of-zhou.s: King Li of Zhou was the tenth king of the Western Zhou dynasty, reigning from about 877 to 841 BCE. His harsh rule, monopolies and suppression of criticism provoked a revolt in the capital in 841 BCE, which drove him into exile at Zhi.

king-zhao-of-chu.s: King Zhao of Chu ruled the State of Chu from 516 to 489 BCE. In 506 BCE the State of Wu, guided by the Chu exile Wu Zixu, defeated Chu at Boju and took its capital Ying, and the king fled to the small state of Sui.

konigsberg.s: Königsberg was a city on the Pregel River near the Baltic coast, founded by the Teutonic Order in 1255 and named in honour of King Ottokar II of Bohemia. It was the seat of the grand masters from 1457, capital of the Duchy of Prussia, coronation city of the Prussian kings and…

king-helu-of-wu.s: Helü was king of Wu from 514 to 496 BCE, after seizing the throne by having his cousin King Liao assassinated. Advised by Wu Zixu and, by tradition, Sun Tzu, he defeated Chu at Boju and took its capital Ying in 506 BCE, making Wu a great power.

king-huan-of-zhou.s: King Huan of Zhou reigned from 719 to 697 BCE as the second king of the Eastern Zhou. Trying to assert royal authority over the State of Zheng, he led an army against Duke Zhuang of Zheng in 707 BCE and was defeated at Xuge, where an arrow struck his shoulder.

korana.s: The Korana are a Khoikhoi people of the interior of South Africa, who moved north from the Cape into the Orange and Vaal river valleys in the 18th century. Living by herding, hunting and raiding on horseback, their groups fought Tswana, Griqua and settler neighbours.

kaihuang-code.s: The Kaihuang Code was the law code of the Sui dynasty, issued by Emperor Wen in 581 and revised in 583, during the Kaihuang era. It reduced the number of capital offences and harsh punishments and arranged the law in twelve sections with five standard punishments.

kaykhusraw-i.s: Kaykhusraw I was sultan of the Seljuk Sultanate of Rum in Anatolia, reigning from 1192 to 1196 and again from 1205 to 1211. The youngest son of Kilij Arslan II, he lost the throne to his brother Suleiman II before regaining it, and took the port of Antalya in 1207.

khadija-of-the-maldives.s: Khadija was sultana of the Maldives, reigning three times between 1347 and 1380 and twice deposing husbands who had seized power. The daughter of Sultan Omar I, she was ruling when Ibn Battuta served as a judge in Male in the 1340s, and he described her court.

kartasura.s: Kartasura is a town in Central Java, Indonesia, just west of Surakarta. Amangkurat II built it as the new capital of the Mataram Sultanate in 1680 after the Trunajaya rebellion.

krishna.s: Krishna is one of the most widely worshipped Hindu gods, revered as an avatar of Vishnu or as the supreme deity. In the Mahabharata he is the Yadava prince who counsels Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gita, and later texts celebrate his childhood among the cowherds around Mathura.

krishna-river.s: The Krishna is one of the major rivers of peninsular India, flowing about 1,300 kilometres from the Western Ghats in Maharashtra east across Karnataka, Telangana and Andhra Pradesh to the Bay of Bengal. Its fertile lower valley and delta supported the Satavahanas, the…

kawar-people.s: The Kawar, also written Kanwar, are an Adivasi people of Chhattisgarh in central India, living mainly in the northern districts such as Korba, Surguja, Bilaspur and Jashpur. Traditionally settled farmers, they claim descent from the Kauravas of the Mahabharata and speak…

karlstad-convention.s: The Karlstad Convention was the set of agreements negotiated at Karlstad, Sweden, in September 1905 that settled the peaceful dissolution of the union between Sweden and Norway. After Norway's Storting declared the union ended and a referendum endorsed it, the two countries…

kingisepp.s: Kingisepp is a town in Leningrad Oblast, Russia, on the Luga River. It began as Yam, a stone fortress built by Novgorod in 1384 to guard its north-western frontier.

koporye.s: Koporye is a village in Leningrad Oblast, Russia, known for its medieval fortress. The Teutonic Knights first built a fort there in 1240, and Novgorod built the stone fortress in the late 13th century to defend its lands on the Gulf of Finland.

kinnaird-head.s: Kinnaird Head is a headland at Fraserburgh on the north-east corner of Aberdeenshire, Scotland, where the coast turns west along the Moray Firth. It is usually identified with the Taexalorum Promontorium, the headland of the Taexali, in Ptolemy's Geography.

kankuamo-people.s: The Kankuamo are an Indigenous people of the south-eastern slopes of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in northern Colombia, one of the four peoples who regard themselves as heirs of the Tairona. They largely lost their language and customs under colonial and later pressure,…

kogi-people.s: The Kogi are an Indigenous people of the northern Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in Colombia, speaking a Chibchan language and widely regarded as heirs of the Tairona. Led by spiritual authorities called mamos, they see themselves as guardians of the balance of the world.

kodama-gentaro.s: Kodama Gentarō (1852–1906) was a Japanese general and statesman. As Governor-General of Taiwan from 1898 to 1906, with Gotō Shinpei as his civil administrator, he consolidated colonial control and promoted the island's economic development.

khujand.s: Khujand is the second city of Tajikistan, on the Syr Darya at the entrance to the Fergana Valley. One of the oldest towns of Central Asia, it is identified with Alexandria Eschate, founded by Alexander the Great in 329 BCE, and was a station on the Silk Road.

kulob.s: Kulob is a city in Khatlon province in southern Tajikistan, centre of a historic region east of the Vakhsh river. Once a province of the Emirate of Bukhara, the region was in the civil war of 1992–1997 the base of the Popular Front that brought Emomali Rahmon, a native of the…

kagawa-prefecture.s: Kagawa Prefecture is the smallest prefecture of Japan, in the north-east of Shikoku on the Seto Inland Sea, with its capital at Takamatsu. It corresponds to the old province of Sanuki, divided in the Edo period mainly between the Takamatsu and Marugame domains.

kofu.s: Kōfu is the capital of Yamanashi Prefecture, Japan, in a basin west of Tokyo. It grew from 1519 around the Tsutsujigasaki residence of the Takeda clan, rulers of Kai Province.

kozuke-province.s: Kōzuke Province was an old province of Japan in the northern Kanto region, now Gunma Prefecture. In the Sengoku period it was contested by the Uesugi, Takeda and Later Hōjō, and under the Tokugawa it was divided among several domains, including Maebashi and Takasaki.

karaeng-pattingalloang.s: Karaeng Pattingalloang (1600–1654) was a nobleman of Tallo and chancellor of the twin kingdom of Gowa–Tallo in South Sulawesi from 1639. Famous among European visitors for his learning, he read Portuguese and Spanish, collected European books and maps, and ordered a large…

kalhora-dynasty.s: The Kalhora dynasty ruled Sindh from about 1701 to 1783, first as governors under the Mughals and later as tributaries of Nader Shah and the Durrani rulers. Of Sufi origins, the Kalhoras built canals and founded Hyderabad as their capital in 1768.

ketapang.s: Ketapang is a town and regency on the south-west coast of West Kalimantan, on the Indonesian part of Borneo. The area was the centre of the old kingdom of Tanjungpura, listed in the Nagarakretagama of 1365 among the dependencies of Majapahit, and later of the sultanate of Matan.

kizildag.s: Kızıldağ is a rocky hill on the Konya plain in south-central Turkey, once an island in a lake that has since dried up. It bears Luwian hieroglyphic inscriptions and a carved image of the great king Hartapu, among the main records of the rulers who held the region of…

kurunta.s: Kurunta was a Hittite prince, son of Muwatalli II, who ruled the appanage kingdom of Tarhuntassa in southern Anatolia in the 13th century BCE. His treaty with the great king Tudhaliya IV, inscribed on a bronze tablet found at Hattusa in 1986, sets out his borders and privileges.

kickapoo.s: The Kickapoo are an Algonquian-speaking Native American people who in the 17th and 18th centuries lived in the region of present-day Wisconsin, Illinois and Indiana. Many joined Tecumseh's confederacy against American expansion.

kasi-viswanathar-temple-tenkasi.s: The Kasi Viswanathar Temple is a Hindu temple to Shiva at Tenkasi in Tamil Nadu, India. It was begun in the 1440s by the Pandya king Arikesari Parakrama Pandya, and the town's name, 'Southern Kashi', recalls the sacred city of Varanasi, whose temple of Vishwanath it was meant…

kizlyar.s: Kizlyar is a town in northern Dagestan, Russia, on the lower Terek River near the Caspian Sea. Founded as a Russian fortress in 1735, it anchored the eastern end of the Caucasian fortified line and became a trading town with Armenian and Georgian merchants, known for its wine…

kokoda-track-campaign.s: The Kokoda Track campaign was fought between July and November 1942 in the Owen Stanley Range of Papua, then an Australian territory. Japanese forces advancing overland towards Port Moresby were halted and pushed back by Australian troops, helped by Papuan carriers.

kurukshetra.s: Kurukshetra is a city and district in Haryana, northern India, north of Delhi. In Hindu tradition it is the battlefield of the Mahabharata war and the place where Krishna taught the Bhagavad Gita, and its sacred tanks, such as Brahma Sarovar, draw pilgrims.

kumbakonam.s: Kumbakonam is a temple town in the Thanjavur district of Tamil Nadu, India, between the Kaveri and Arasalar rivers. An important centre under the Cholas and later the Nayaks and Marathas of Thanjavur, it is known for its many Hindu temples and for the Mahamaham festival, held…

khababash.s: Khababash was an Egyptian ruler who led a revolt against Persian rule in the Nile Delta in the late 330s BCE, probably during the turmoil that followed the murders of Artaxerxes III and Artaxerxes IV. He is known from a few documents, including the Satrap Stela of Ptolemy I,…

kieu-cong-tien.s: Kieu Cong Tien was a Vietnamese commander who in 937 murdered Duong Dinh Nghe, the governor of the Tinh Hai circuit who had expelled the Southern Han, and took power himself. Facing a campaign of revenge by Nghe's son-in-law Ngo Quyen, he appealed to the Southern Han for help,…

kalasasaya.s: The Kalasasaya is a large rectangular platform enclosure at Tiwanaku, near Lake Titicaca in Bolivia, bounded by walls of tall upright stone pillars. It was probably used for ceremonies and for observing the movements of the sun, and it contains the Ponce and Fraile monoliths.

kinich-baaknal-chaak.s: K'inich B'aaknal Chaak was the ruler of the Maya city of Toniná, in Chiapas, Mexico, from 688 into the early 8th century. He waged repeated wars against the rival kingdom of Palenque, recording victories and captives on carved monuments, and his reign and those of his…

krajina.s: Krajina, meaning 'frontier', is the name given to the former lands of the Habsburg Military Frontier in Croatia, where Serb settlers served as border soldiers against the Ottomans from the 16th century. The Frontier was abolished in 1881, but the Serb communities remained, and…

kamla-persad-bissessar.s: Kamla Persad-Bissessar is a Trinidadian lawyer and politician who became the first woman prime minister of Trinidad and Tobago in 2010, at the head of the People's Partnership coalition. She served until 2015 and returned as prime minister after the 2025 election victory of…

kanchan-prabha-devi.s: Kanchan Prabha Devi was the queen of Maharaja Bir Bikram Kishore Manikya of Tripura. After his death in 1947 she became regent for their young son, Kirit Bikram Kishore Manikya, and headed the council of regency during the partition of India.

khumarawayh.s: Khumarawayh was the second Tulunid ruler of Egypt and Syria, succeeding his father Ahmad ibn Tulun in 884. After fighting the Abbasid regent al-Muwaffaq, he reached a treaty in 886 that recognised his rule over Egypt and Syria in return for tribute.

konstantin-von-kaufmann.s: Konstantin von Kaufmann was a Russian general and the first governor-general of Russian Turkestan, from its creation in 1867 until his death in 1882. From Tashkent he directed the conquest of Samarkand in 1868, made the Emirate of Bukhara and the Khanate of Khiva protectorates…

karakum-canal.s: The Karakum Canal is one of the longest irrigation canals in the world, carrying water from the Amu Darya westward across the Karakum desert of Turkmenistan. Construction began in 1954, and over the following decades it was extended for about 1,300 kilometres past Ashgabat.

kallar.s: Kallar was a Brahmin minister of the last Turk Shahi king of Kabul who, according to the 11th-century scholar al-Biruni, overthrew his master and founded the Hindu Shahi dynasty in the 9th century. His dynasty ruled Kabul and Gandhara, later from Udabhandapura on the Indus,…

king-hancock.s: King Hancock was a Tuscarora leader in North Carolina, chief of the southern Tuscarora towns around Catechna. Angered by settler encroachment, land seizures and the enslavement of their people, his warriors attacked the colonial settlements on the Neuse and Pamlico rivers in…

kaqchikel-people.s: The Kaqchikel are a Maya people of the central highlands of Guatemala. Once allies and subjects of the K'iche', their lords broke away around 1470 and founded their own capital at Iximche, from which they fought the K'iche' and Tz'utujil.

kasugayama-castle.s: Kasugayama Castle was a mountain castle near modern Jōetsu in Niigata Prefecture, Japan, and the seat of Uesugi Kenshin in the 16th century. From it the Nagao and Uesugi lords controlled Echigo Province.

konrad-von-heresbach.s: Konrad von Heresbach was a German humanist, jurist and agricultural writer, a friend of Erasmus and tutor to the future Duke William of Jülich-Cleves-Berg. As counsellor to Duke John III he shaped a moderate, Erasmian church policy that sought reform without breaking with Rome.

koza-riot.s: The Koza riot was an outbreak of violence in the city of Koza, now Okinawa City, on the night of 20 December 1970, during the American administration of Okinawa. After a traffic accident in which an American serviceman hit a local man, a crowd of thousands attacked US military…

kullaba.s: Kullaba was one of the two original settlements that grew together to form the Sumerian city of Uruk in the 4th millennium BCE, alongside Eanna. It contained the sanctuary of the sky god An, with the White Temple on its high terrace.

kyzyl.s: Kyzyl is the capital of the Republic of Tuva in southern Siberia, Russia, on the upper Yenisei river. It was founded by the Russians in 1914 as Belotsarsk, the administrative centre of the Uryankhay Krai, and was later renamed Kyzyl, 'red', as the capital of the Tuvan People's…

kilkenny.s: Kilkenny is a city in south-east Ireland on the River Nore, the county town of County Kilkenny. It grew around a monastery of St Canice, from whom its Irish name Cill Chainnigh comes, and became the seat of the bishops of Ossory.

kutrigurs.s: The Kutrigurs were a Turkic nomadic people of the Pontic steppe west of the Don in the 6th century, closely related to the Utigurs to the east. They raided the Balkans repeatedly, and in 559 their leader Zabergan reached the walls of Constantinople before being driven off by…

kabah.s: Kabah is a Maya archaeological site in the Puuc hills of Yucatán, Mexico, about 20 km south-east of Uxmal, to which it was linked by a raised causeway (sacbe) ending in a free-standing arch. It flourished in the 9th and 10th centuries.

kerei-khan.s: Kerei Khan was a descendant of Urus Khan of the White Horde and, with Janibek Khan, the founder of the Kazakh Khanate. In the mid-15th century the two led discontented clans away from Abu'l-Khayr Khan's Uzbek confederation to the Chu valley, under the protection of the khans…

khambhat.s: Khambhat, historically Cambay, is a town in Gujarat, India, at the head of the Gulf of Khambhat. From the medieval period it was one of the great ports of western India, exporting textiles, indigo and beads across the Indian Ocean, and it was visited by Marco Polo and many…

kamala-devi.s: Kamala Devi was the queen of Karna, the last Vaghela king of Gujarat. When the armies of Alauddin Khalji sacked Gujarat in 1299 she was captured and taken to Delhi, where she became one of Alauddin's wives.

karna-vaghela.s: Karna, also called Karnadeva, was the last Vaghela king of Gujarat. In 1299 the Delhi sultan Alauddin Khalji sent his generals Ulugh Khan and Nusrat Khan against him; they sacked the capital Anahilavada and plundered the temple of Somnath, and Karna fled while his queen Kamala…

kythira.s: Kythira is a Greek island off the south-eastern tip of the Peloponnese, at the meeting of the Ionian and Aegean seas. In antiquity it was sacred to Aphrodite.

koroni.s: Koroni is a small port town in Messenia, on the south-western coast of the Peloponnese in Greece, guarded by a medieval fortress. Held by Venice from about 1207 to 1500 as Coron, it was, with nearby Modon, one of the 'eyes of the Republic', a vital port of call on the sea…

kinross-shire.s: Kinross-shire is a historic county of central Scotland, one of the smallest in the country, centred on the town of Kinross and Loch Leven, where Mary, Queen of Scots was imprisoned in 1567–1568. Lying between Fife and Perthshire, it is now part of the Perth and Kinross council…

kaupang.s: Kaupang was a Viking Age trading town near Larvik in Vestfold, Norway, occupied from about 800 to the mid-10th century. It is usually identified with Sciringes heal, the port described by the Norwegian traveller Ohthere to King Alfred of Wessex.

kuzi-teshub.s: Kuzi-Teshub was a ruler of Carchemish in northern Syria, son of Talmi-Teshub, the last Hittite viceroy there. After the collapse of the Hittite Empire around 1180 BCE he took the title 'Great King', and his descendants ruled Carchemish and the kingdom of Melid (Malatya),…

kuito.s: Kuito is the capital of Bié Province in the central highlands of Angola. It grew on the lands of the Viye kingdom and in the colonial period was named Silva Porto after the Portuguese trader who had lived there.

klyazma.s: The Klyazma is a river of central Russia, about 690 km long, rising north-west of Moscow and flowing east past Vladimir to join the Oka near Gorokhovets. Its valley was the heart of the principality of Vladimir-Suzdal, whose capital Vladimir and towns such as Bogolyubovo and…

kama-river.s: The Kama is the largest left-bank tributary of the Volga, about 1,800 km long, rising in the uplands of Udmurtia in Russia and flowing past Perm to join the Volga below Kazan. The land around its confluence with the Volga was the heartland of Volga Bulgaria, and its upper…

kuksha.s: Kuksha was a monk of the Kiev Monastery of the Caves who preached Christianity to the pagan Vyatichi in the late 11th or early 12th century and was killed by them together with his disciple Nikon. Venerated as a martyr, he is a saint of the Orthodox Church, and his relics are…

kirov.s: Kirov is a city on the Vyatka river in north-eastern European Russia, the centre of Kirov Oblast. First reliably recorded in the 14th century as Khlynov, the main town of the Vyatka land settled from Novgorod, it was annexed by Moscow in 1489.

kingdom-of-alo.s: Alo is one of the two traditional kingdoms of the island of Futuna in the French Pacific territory of Wallis and Futuna, covering the eastern part of Futuna and the neighbouring island of Alofi. Its king, the Tu'i Agaifo, is chosen from noble families.

kingdom-of-sigave.s: Sigave is one of the two traditional kingdoms of the island of Futuna in Wallis and Futuna, covering the western part of the island around the village of Leava. Its king, the Tu'i Sigave, is chosen by the noble families.

kalenjin-people.s: The Kalenjin are a group of related Nilotic-speaking peoples of the highlands of western Kenya's Rift Valley, among them the Nandi, Kipsigis, Keiyo, Marakwet and Tugen. Traditionally cattle-keepers and farmers organised in age sets, they speak closely related languages.

kapp-putsch.s: The Kapp Putsch was an attempted coup against the Weimar Republic in March 1920, led by Wolfgang Kapp and General Walther von Lüttwitz with Freikorps troops due to be disbanded under the Treaty of Versailles. The rebels occupied Berlin and the government fled, but most of the…

kolar.s: Kolar is a city in south-eastern Karnataka, India, east of Bangalore. As Kuvalala it was the early capital of the Western Ganga dynasty before they moved to Talakad, and the region was later held by the Nolambas, the Cholas and Vijayanagara.

kardamaka-dynasty.s: The Kardamaka dynasty was the main line of the Western Satraps, Saka rulers of western India, founded by Chastana at Ujjain in the early 2nd century CE. Its kings, including Rudradaman I, ruled Gujarat, Malwa and neighbouring regions and issued a long, dated series of silver…

king-you-of-zhou.s: King You of Zhou was the last king of the Western Zhou dynasty, reigning from 781 to 771 BCE. He set aside his queen, a daughter of the Marquis of Shen, and their son in favour of his consort Bao Si and her son.

kirn.s: Kirn is a town on the Nahe River in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany, at the edge of the Hunsrück hills. Above it stands the ruined Kyrburg castle, a seat of the Wild- and Rhinegraves and of their successors, the Princes of Salm-Kyrburg, who ruled the town until the French…

kyrburg.s: Kyrburg is a ruined castle on a hill above the town of Kirn on the Nahe in Rhineland-Palatinate, Germany. First recorded in the 12th century, it passed to the Wildgraves and later to the Wild- and Rhinegraves, and it gave its name to the princely line of Salm-Kyrburg.

kebineng.s: Kebineng (died 235) was a Xianbei chieftain who rebuilt a large confederation on the northern frontier of China after the break-up of Tanshihuai's realm. Aided by Chinese refugees, he adopted Chinese-style weapons, armour and organisation, and by the 220s controlled lands from…

kartikeya.s: Kartikeya, also called Skanda, Murugan and Subrahmanya, is the Hindu god of war, son of Shiva and Parvati and commander of the army of the gods. Widely worshipped in ancient India, he was the patron deity of the Yaudheya republic and appears on Kushan and Gupta coins.

kinich-tatbu-skull-iv.s: K'inich Tatbu Skull IV was the last known king of the Maya city of Yaxchilan, recorded on Lintel 10 around 808. That inscription records his capture of K'inich Yat Ahk II, the last known king of the rival city of Piedras Negras.

khakas-people.s: The Khakas are a Turkic people of southern Siberia living mainly in the Republic of Khakassia, in the Minusinsk Basin on the upper Yenisei River in Russia. They are often linked to the medieval Yenisei Kyrgyz, whose khaganate ruled the Mongolian steppe in the 9th century.

korla.s: Korla is a city in central Xinjiang, China, on the north-eastern edge of the Tarim Basin at the foot of the Tian Shan, and the seat of the Bayingolin Mongol Autonomous Prefecture. An ancient oasis on the northern Silk Road, it is where Yaqub Beg, ruler of Yettishar, died in…

kumo-xi.s: The Kumo Xi, or Xi, were a nomadic people of the upper Liao River region of eastern Inner Mongolia, closely related to the Khitan and traced by Chinese sources to the Yuwen Xianbei. They were subject in turn to the Turks, the Tang and the Uyghurs, and from the 10th century…

kaduna-state.s: Kaduna State is a state of north-western Nigeria, with its capital at Kaduna, the former administrative centre of colonial Northern Nigeria. It took its present name in 1976 and its present borders in 1987, when Katsina State was separated from it.

khotogoid.s: The Khotogoid were a Mongol people of north-western Mongolia, part of the western Khalkha domain under the Zasagt Khan. Their princes took the title Altan Khan in the late sixteenth and seventeenth centuries, exchanged embassies with Russia and fought the Oirats for the lands…

khyunglung.s: Khyunglung is a valley on the upper Sutlej river in Ngari, western Tibet, west of Mount Kailash. Its cave complex and ruins, Khyunglung Ngulkhar, the "Silver Castle of the Garuda Valley", are identified in Bon tradition as the capital of the ancient kingdom of Zhangzhung, and…

king-cuo-of-zhongshan.s: King Cuo was a ruler of the state of Zhongshan in present-day Hebei, China, in the late fourth century BCE, and the first of its rulers to take the title of king, in 323 BCE. His tomb near Pingshan, excavated in the 1970s, yielded bronze vessels with long inscriptions, inlaid…

king-wuling-of-zhao.s: King Wuling of Zhao ruled the state of Zhao in northern China from 325 to 299 BCE. In 307 BCE he ordered his army to adopt the trousers and mounted archery of the steppe nomads, a reform that made Zhao a leading military power, and he conquered the state of Zhongshan, whose…

keikavus.s: Keikavus, or Kai Kavus ibn Iskandar, was a Ziyarid prince of the Caspian region in the eleventh century and a grandson of Qabus ibn Vushmgir. He is known as the author of the Qabus-nama, written in 1082 to 1083 for his son Gilanshah, a Persian book of advice on ethics,…

kazakh-dzungar-wars.s: The Kazakh–Dzungar wars were a series of conflicts from the 1640s to the 1750s between the Kazakh Khanate and the Dzungar Khanate for the steppes of Central Asia. The Dzungar invasion of 1723, remembered by Kazakhs as the 'Years of Great Disaster', drove many Kazakhs from…
